claims.statement_id: Kisah lain menyatakan bahwa Abere menciptakan dugong pertama dengan menarik seorang bayi ke dalam air dan mengubahnya sebelum tenggelam, sehingga sang ibu menyusul dan ikut berubah.
claims.quote: A separate story says that Abere created the first dugongs by pulling an infant into the water and transforming it before it drowned, causing the mother to follow and be transformed as well.

claims.statement: Once they are trapped, she proceeds to devour her victims.
claims.statement_id: Setelah mereka terperangkap, ia memangsa korbannya.
claims.quote: Once they are trapped, she proceeds to devour her victims.

claims.statement: This source describes a song relating the building and destruction of a darimo on the mainland opposite the island of Kiwai (where the song was sung) and the party's subsequent adventures, and calls Abere their "Culture Heroine".
claims.statement_id: Sumber ini menyebut sebuah lagu yang menceritakan pembangunan dan pembongkaran sebuah darimo di daratan seberang pulau Kiwai (tempat lagu itu dinyanyikan) serta petualangan rombongan selanjutnya, dan menyebut Abere sebagai "Culture Heroine" mereka.
claims.quote: relating the building and destruction of a darimo on the mainland opposite the island of Kiwai (where the song was sung) ... of their Culture Heroine, Abere, and the subsequent adventures of the party

claims.statement: In Aboriginal cultures of south-east Australia, Daramulum is a sky hero associated with Baiame and an emu-wife, and is described as a shapeshifter.
claims.statement_id: Dalam budaya Aboriginal di Australia tenggara, Daramulum adalah pahlawan langit yang dikaitkan dengan Baiame dan seorang istri emu; ia disebut pengubah wujud.
claims.quote: In Aboriginal cultures of south-east Australia, Daramulum ... is a sky hero associated with Baiame, and an emu-wife. He is a shapeshifter.

claims.statement: Daramulum is depicted in semi-profile with one arm, an emu-back (pointed buttocks), and a large foot.
claims.statement_id: Daramulum digambarkan dalam setengah profil dengan satu lengan, punggung emu (bokong runcing), dan kaki besar.
claims.quote: He is depicted in semi-profile, with one arm, an emu-back (i.e. pointed buttocks), and a large foot.

claims.statement: His voice is heard through the bullroarer whirled during initiation ceremonies.
claims.statement_id: Suara Daramulum terdengar melalui dengungan bullroarer dalam upacara inisiasi.
claims.quote: His voice can be heard through the medium of the bullroarer which is whirled through the air during initiation ceremonies.

claims.statement: Daramulum is depicted on rock art off Elvina Track in Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park, near to a carving of his emu-wife.
claims.statement_id: Daramulum digambarkan pada seni cadas di dekat Elvina Track di Taman Nasional Ku-ring-gai Chase, dekat ukiran istri emu-nya.
claims.quote: Daramulum is depicted on rock art off Elvina Track in Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park, near to a carving of his emu-wife.

claims.statement: For the Guringai, Daramulum is represented by Alpha Crucis of the Southern Cross, with the rest of the Cross representing the head of his emu wife.
claims.statement_id: Bagi suku Guringai, Daramulum diwakili oleh bintang Alpha Crucis dari Salib Selatan, dan sisa rasi itu melambangkan kepala istri emu-nya.
claims.quote: For the Guringai, Daramulum is represented by the Alpha Crucis of the Southern Cross, with the remainder of the Cross representing the head of his emu wife

claims.statement: A religion centred on Darhumulan (a variant spelling of the name) is an identifying feature of the Yuin nation.
claims.statement_id: Agama yang berpusat pada Darhumulan (ejaan lain nama ini) menjadi ciri pengenal bangsa Yuin.
claims.quote: A religion centred on Darhumulan is an identifying feature of the Yuin nation.

claims.statement: Belief in Daramulun, the "father", and Biamban, the "master", is shared by all the tribes who attend the Yuin Kuringal.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan kepada Daramulun, sang "bapa", dan Biamban, sang "tuan", dimiliki semua suku yang menghadiri Kuringal Yuin.
claims.quote: The belief in Daramulun, the " father," and Biamban, or " master," is common to all of the tribes who attend the Yuin Kuringal.

claims.statement: The Yuin believe that thunder is the voice of Daramulun.
claims.statement_id: Suku Yuin percaya bahwa guntur adalah suara Daramulun.
claims.quote: The Yuin believe that the thunder is the voice of Daramulun.

claims.statement: The Ngarigo also thought that the spirit of a dead person went up to the sky, where it was met by Daramulun, who, as an old Ngarigo man said, takes care of it.
claims.statement_id: Suku Ngarigo juga mengira roh orang mati naik ke langit, tempat ia disambut Daramulun, yang menurut seorang tetua Ngarigo merawatnya.
claims.quote: Their neighbours the Ngarigo also thought that the spirit of a dead person ... went up to the sky, where it was met by Daramulun, who, as one of the old Ngarigo men said, takes care of it.

claims.statement: The medicine-man is everywhere believed to have received his dreaded power from a supernatural source or being such as Baiame, Daramulun or Bunjil, or from the ancestral ghosts.
claims.statement_id: Dukun (medicine-man) di mana-mana dipercaya menerima kekuatannya dari sumber atau makhluk gaib seperti Baiame, Daramulun, atau Bunjil, atau dari hantu leluhur.
claims.quote: The general belief as to the powers of the medicine-man are much the same in all the tribes herein spoken of. He is everywhere believed to have received his dreaded power from some supernatural source, or being, such as Baiame, Daramulun, or Bunjil, or the ancestral ghosts.

claims.statement: According to this passage, Daramulun lives in such places, namely a tree with a great swelling round its roots.
claims.statement_id: Menurut bagian ini, Daramulun tinggal di tempat-tempat semacam itu, yaitu pohon dengan pembengkakan besar di sekeliling akarnya.
claims.quote: a tree with a great swelling round its roots. It is in such places that Daramulun lives.

claims.statement: In this passage a figure of Daramulun is cut on the ground; here he is not the Supernatural Being of the Yuin beliefs but the "boy", or son, of Baiame, and is always shown with one leg, the other ending in a sharp point of bone.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bagian ini, figur Daramulun digambar di tanah; ia di sini bukan Makhluk Gaib dalam kepercayaan Yuin melainkan "anak" atau putra Baiame, dan selalu digambarkan berkaki satu dengan ujung lainnya runcing dari tulang.
claims.quote: they cut on the ground the figure of Daramulun, who is not the Supernatural Being of the Yuin beliefs, but the " boy," or son, of Baiame. He is always represented as having only one leg, the other terminating in a sharp point of bone.

claims.statement: Also figured on the ground are the tomahawk Daramulun let fall as he slipped down from the tree to the ground, and two emu footprints made when the emu tried to escape from Daramulun.
claims.statement_id: Di tanah juga digambar kapak yang dijatuhkan Daramulun ketika ia meluncur turun dari pohon ke tanah, lalu dua jejak kaki emu yang dibuat saat mencoba lolos dari Daramulun.
claims.quote: There is also figured on the ground the tomahawk which Daramulun let fall as he slipped down from the tree before mentioned to the ground ; then two footprints of an emu a little distance from each other, made when trying to escape from Daramulun.

claims.statement: The boys are told that Daramulun will injure or kill them with stones heated in the fire if they tell any of the secrets.
claims.statement_id: Anak-anak laki-laki diberi tahu bahwa Daramulun akan melukai atau membunuh mereka dengan batu yang dipanaskan di api jika mereka membocorkan rahasia.
claims.quote: to imitate the bursting of stones heated in the fire, with which the boys are told Daramulun will injure or kill them if they tell any of the secrets.

claims.statement: Howitt writes that there is not any worship of Daramulun.
claims.statement_id: Howitt menulis bahwa tidak ada pemujaan terhadap Daramulun.
claims.quote: There is not any worship of Daramulun

claims.statement: Howitt concludes that Nurrundere, Nurelli, Bunjil, Mungan-ngaua, Daramulun and Baianie all represent the same being under different names.
claims.statement_id: Howitt menyimpulkan bahwa Nurrundere, Nurelli, Bunjil, Mungan-ngaua, Daramulun, dan Baianie semuanya mewakili satu sosok yang sama dengan nama berbeda.
claims.quote: It seems quite clear that Nurrundere, Nurelli, Bunjil, Mungan-ngaua, Daramulun, and Baianie all represent the same being under different names.

claims.statement: Degei, enshrined as a serpent, is the supreme deity of Fiji.
claims.statement_id: Degei yang berwujud ular adalah dewa tertinggi dalam mitologi Fiji.
claims.quote: In Fijian mythology, Degei (pronounced Ndengei), enshrined as a serpent, is the supreme god of Fiji.

claims.statement: He is the creator of the world, fruits, and humans in Fiji.
claims.statement_id: Degei adalah pencipta bumi, buah-buahan, dan manusia di Fiji.
claims.quote: He is the creator of the (Fijian) world, fruits, and of men and is specially connected to Rakiraki District, Fiji.

claims.statement: He judges departed souls after they pass through Cibaciba or Drakulu caves.
claims.statement_id: Degei mengadili jiwa-jiwa yang baru wafat setelah melewati gua Cibaciba atau Drakulu.
claims.quote: He judges newly dead souls after they pass through one of two caves: Cibaciba or Drakulu.

claims.statement: He is said to have first moved about freely, but then, in snake form, to have grown into the earth with his ringed tail; since then he has become the god of earthquakes, storms and seasons.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikatakan mula-mula bergerak bebas, tetapi lalu dalam wujud ular tumbuh menyatu dengan bumi bersama ekornya yang berlingkar; sejak itu ia menjadi dewa gempa bumi, badai, dan musim.
claims.quote: He is said to have at first moved about freely, but then in the form of a snake to have grown into the earth with his ringed tail. Since then he has become the god of earthquakes, storms and seasons.

claims.statement: Whenever Degei shakes himself, fertilising rain falls, delicious fruits hang on the trees and the yam fields yield an excellent crop.
claims.statement_id: Setiap kali Degei mengguncang dirinya, hujan penyubur turun, buah-buahan lezat bergantung di pohon, dan ladang ubi memberi hasil yang sangat baik.
claims.quote: Whenever Degei shakes himself fertilising rain will fall, delicious fruits hang on the trees, and the yam fields yield an excellent crop.

claims.statement: Degei is also a god of wrath who declares himself in terrible fashion; he punishes his people by destroying the crops or by floods, and having lived in the bowels of the earth he is tormented by so insatiable a hunger that he would like to swallow the whole world.
claims.statement_id: Degei juga dewa murka yang menyatakan diri secara mengerikan; ia menghukum umatnya dengan merusak panen atau dengan banjir, dan karena tinggal di perut bumi ia disiksa lapar yang tak terpuaskan sehingga ingin menelan seluruh dunia.
claims.quote: Degei is also a god of wrath who declares himself in terrible fashion. He punishes and chastens his people by destroying the crops or by floods; he could indeed easily wipe out mankind from the earth, for since he has lived in the bowels of the earth he has been tormented with so insatiable hunger that he would like to take in and swallow the whole world.

claims.statement: Rokola is a name of the son of Degei.
claims.statement_id: Rokola adalah nama putra Degei.
claims.quote: Rokola is a name of the son of Degei.

claims.statement: In these traditions Degei figures not only as the origin of the people but also as a huge snake living in a cave near the summit of the mountain Uluda, the northernmost peak of the Nakauvandra Range.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi-tradisi ini Degei tampil bukan hanya sebagai asal usul manusia, tetapi juga sebagai ular raksasa yang tinggal di gua dekat puncak gunung Uluda, puncak paling utara Pegunungan Nakauvandra.
claims.quote: In these traditions Degei figures not only as the origin of the people, but also as a huge snake, living in a cave near the summit of the mountain Uluda - the northernmost peak of the Nakauvandra Range.

claims.statement: According to the passage quoted on this page, he took no interest in his people's affairs; his existence was no more than a round of eating and sleeping.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kutipan di halaman ini, ia tidak tertarik pada urusan umatnya; keberadaannya hanya berputar pada makan dan tidur.
claims.quote: In these traditions Degei figures not only as the origin of the people, but also as a huge snake ... He took no interest in his people's affairs; his existence was no more than a round of eating and sleeping.

claims.statement: The god most generally known in Fiji is Ndengei, who seems to be an impersonation of the abstract idea of eternal existence.
claims.statement_id: Dewa yang paling dikenal di Fiji adalah Ndengei, yang tampaknya merupakan personifikasi gagasan abstrak tentang keberadaan abadi.
claims.quote: The god most generally known in Fiji is Ndengei, who seems to be an impersonation of the abstract idea of eternal existence.

claims.statement: The serpent, the world-wide symbol of eternity, is his adopted shrine; some traditions represent him with the head and part of the body of that reptile, the rest of his form being stone.
claims.statement_id: Ular, lambang keabadian di seluruh dunia, adalah kuil pilihannya; sebagian tradisi menggambarkannya dengan kepala dan sebagian tubuh ular sedangkan sisanya batu.
claims.quote: The serpent - the world-wide symbol of eternity - is his adopted shrine. Some traditions represent him with the head and part of the body of that reptile, the rest of his form being stone

claims.statement: He passes a monotonous existence in a gloomy cavern, the hollow of an inland rock near the north-east end of Viti Levu, showing no interest in anyone but his attendant Uto, and giving no sign of life beyond eating, answering his priest and changing his position from side to side.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjalani hidup monoton di gua suram, rongga batu pedalaman dekat ujung timur laut Viti Levu, tidak peduli pada siapa pun selain pelayannya Uto, dan hanya makan, menjawab imamnya, dan berganti posisi dari satu sisi ke sisi lain.
claims.quote: He passes a monotonous existence in a gloomy cavern - the hollow of an inland rock near the N. E. end of Viti Levu - evincing no interest in any one but his attendant, Uto, and giving no signs of life beyond eating, answering his priest, and changing his position from one side to the other.

claims.statement: Although Ndengei ranks as supreme among the gods, he has scarcely a temple except about Rakiraki.
claims.statement_id: Meski Ndengei dianggap tertinggi di antara para dewa, di luar sekitar Rakiraki ia nyaris tidak punya kuil.
claims.quote: All though Ndengei ranks as supreme among the gods ... Except about Rakiraki, he has scarcely a temple

claims.statement: Tokairambe and Tui Lakemba Randinandina seem to stand next to Ndengei, being his sons, and act as mediators.
claims.statement_id: Tokairambe dan Tui Lakemba Randinandina tampaknya berkedudukan tepat di bawah Ndengei sebagai putra-putranya dan bertindak sebagai perantara.
claims.quote: Tokairambe and Tui Lakemba Randinandina seem to stand next to Ndengei, being his sons, and acting as mediators

claims.statement: On the day of offering a priest entered the sacred cave where Ndengei dwelt, taking with him what the occasion required.
claims.statement_id: Pada hari persembahan, seorang imam masuk ke gua suci tempat Ndengei bersemayam sambil membawa apa yang dibutuhkan upacara.
claims.quote: On the day of offering a priest entered the sacred cave where Ndengei dwelt, taking with him what the occasion required.

claims.statement: If rain was wanted, the bete (priest) would return dripping from Ndengei with a promise of showers on the district after two or four days; if success in war was asked, a fire-brand was darted from the cave as a token that they should burn up their enemies.
claims.statement_id: Bila hujan diminta, bete (imam) kembali basah kuyup dari Ndengei dengan janji hujan dalam dua atau empat hari; bila diminta kemenangan perang, sebatang bara dilemparkan dari gua sebagai tanda musuh akan dibakar habis.
claims.quote: If rain was wanted, the bete would return dripping with rain from Ndengei, and with a promise that he would thus bestow showers on all the district after two or four days. If they asked success in war, a fire-brand was darted from the cave ; a token that they should burn up their enemies.

claims.statement: The custom of tattooing is said to be in conformity with the appointment of Ndengei, and its neglect punished after death.
claims.statement_id: Adat merajah tubuh konon sesuai dengan ketetapan Ndengei, dan pengabaiannya dihukum setelah mati.
claims.quote: The custom of tattooing is said to be in conformity with the appointment of Ndengei, and its neglect punished after death.

claims.statement: In Fiji it is said that a bird laid two eggs that were hatched by Ndengei, the great serpent, a boy coming from one and a girl from the other.
claims.statement_id: Di Fiji dikatakan seekor burung bertelur dua yang dierami oleh Ndengei, sang ular agung; seorang anak laki-laki keluar dari satu telur dan seorang anak perempuan dari yang lain.
claims.quote: At the other extremity of Melanesia, in Fiji, it is said that a bird laid two eggs which were hatched by Ndengei, the great serpent, a boy coming from one and a girl from the other.

claims.statement: He sends a few souls to the paradise Burotu; most others are thrown into a lake, where they eventually sink to the bottom (Murimuria) to be appropriately rewarded or punished.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian kecil arwah ia kirim ke surga Burotu; kebanyakan lainnya dilemparkan ke danau, tempat mereka akhirnya tenggelam ke dasar (Murimuria) untuk diganjar atau dihukum sepantasnya.
claims.quote: A few he sends to paradise Burotu. Most others are thrown into a lake, where they will eventually sink to the bottom (Murimuria) to be appropriately rewarded or punished.

claims.statement: Waitoreke is an otter/beaver-like creature in New Zealand folklore.
claims.statement_id: Waitoreke adalah makhluk mirip berang-berang dalam cerita rakyat Selandia Baru.
claims.quote: Waitoreke, also commonly referred to as the South Island otter, is an otter/beaver-like creature in New Zealand folklore.

claims.statement: It is described as a small otter-like animal living in the South Island of New Zealand.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini digambarkan sebagai hewan mirip berang-berang kecil di Pulau Selatan Selandia Baru.
claims.quote: In its rare inferred sightings it is usually described as a small otter-like animal that lives in the South Island of New Zealand.

claims.statement: There are many theories on the waitoreke's true identity, such as an otter, beaver or pinniped.
claims.statement_id: Ada banyak teori tentang identitas waitoreke yang sebenarnya, misalnya berang-berang (otter), berang-berang kastor (beaver), atau pinnipedia (anjing laut dan sejenisnya).
claims.quote: There are many theories on the waitoreke's true identity, such as it being an otter, beaver or pinniped.

claims.statement: Evidence for the waitoreke is mainly sporadic accounts of an "unidentified amphibious animal" in the South Island spanning well over 200 years.
claims.statement_id: Bukti keberadaan waitoreke terutama berupa laporan sporadis tentang "hewan amfibi tak dikenal" di Pulau Selatan selama lebih dari 200 tahun.
claims.quote: Evidence for the existence of the waitoreke is mainly based on sporadic accounts of an "unidentified amphibious animal" in the South Island spanning well over 200 years.

claims.statement: The Māori people said that in old times they used to keep waitoreke as pets.
claims.statement_id: Orang Māori mengatakan bahwa pada zaman dahulu mereka memelihara waitoreke sebagai hewan peliharaan.
claims.quote: The Māori people said that in old times they used to keep waitoreke as pets.

claims.statement: Julius von Haast is reported to have obtained a waitoreke pelt in 1868; the fur was brown with white spots and the toes lacked webbing. This is inconclusive, as the pelt seems to have resembled a quoll's.
claims.statement_id: Julius von Haast dilaporkan memperoleh kulit waitoreke pada 1868; bulunya cokelat berbintik putih dan jarinya tanpa selaput. Bukti ini tidak meyakinkan karena kulit itu tampaknya menyerupai kulit quoll.
claims.quote: Julius von Haast is reported to have obtained a waitoreke pelt in 1868. The fur was brown, with white spots, and the toes lacked webbing. This is inconclusive evidence; the pelt seems to have resembled a quoll's.

claims.statement: In a letter dated 6 June 1861, as quoted, Haast wrote that he found the tracks of the vaitoteke (sic) on the upper Ashburton river at 3500 feet; they are similar to an otter's but a bit smaller.
claims.statement_id: Dalam surat bertanggal 6 Juni 1861 yang dikutip, Haast menulis menemukan jejak vaitoteke (sic) di hulu Sungai Ashburton pada ketinggian 3500 kaki; jejaknya mirip jejak berang-berang (otter) tetapi sedikit lebih kecil.
claims.quote: My friend Haast wrote me about vaitoteke (sic) on June 6, 1861: '3500 feet above the sea level I found, on the upper part of Ashburton river (South Island, Canterbury province), in a part of the country which no man has ever visited before me, its tracks. These are similar to those of an otter, only a bit smaller.

claims.statement: The origin of the name "waitoreke" is not well documented; the Rev. Richard Taylor noted its use in the 1840s as "Waitoreke, otter. (Uncertain, perhaps the seal)".
claims.statement_id: Asal nama "waitoreke" tidak terdokumentasi dengan baik; Pdt. Richard Taylor mencatat pemakaiannya pada 1840-an sebagai "Waitoreke, otter. (Uncertain, perhaps the seal)".
claims.quote: The origin of the name "waitoreke" is not well documented; the Rev. Richard Taylor noted its use in the 1840s as "Waitoreke, otter. (Uncertain, perhaps the seal)".

claims.statement: The word does not occur in Tregear's fairly comprehensive Māori dictionary of 1891, and was said to be "ungrammatical" by the leading Māori anthropologist Sir Peter Buck.
claims.statement_id: Kata itu tidak ada dalam kamus Māori Tregear yang cukup lengkap tahun 1891, dan oleh antropolog Māori terkemuka Sir Peter Buck dikatakan "tidak gramatikal".
claims.quote: It does not occur in Tregear's fairly comprehensive Māori dictionary of 1891, and was said to be "ungrammatical" by leading Māori anthropologist Sir Peter Buck.

claims.statement: Other names listed: Kaurehe, Māori otter, New Zealand otter, South Island otter, waitoreki, waitorete.
claims.statement_id: Nama lain yang tercantum: Kaurehe, Māori otter, New Zealand otter, South Island otter, waitoreki, waitorete.
claims.quote: Other name(s) Kaurehe, Māori otter, New Zealand otter, South Island otter, waitoreki, waitorete

claims.statement: Pollock writes that the waitoreke, or supposed South Island otter, has remained a mystery for over a century, and that zoologists generally have been only too happy to dismiss it as a myth.
claims.statement_id: Pollock menulis bahwa waitoreke, atau "berang-berang Pulau Selatan" yang diduga, tetap menjadi misteri lebih dari seabad, dan para zoolog umumnya senang menepisnya sebagai mitos.
claims.quote: The waitoreke, or supposed South Island otter, has remained a mystery for over a century ... zoologists generally have been only too happy to dismiss the animal as a myth.

claims.statement: According to Pollock, Tarawhata in 1848 gave Mantell a description full of otter-like detail: two feet from nose to root of tail, living in holes, with grisly-brown fur, short thick legs, a bushy tail and a head between that of a dog and a cat.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Pollock, Tarawhata pada 1848 memberi Mantell gambaran penuh detail mirip berang-berang (otter): panjang dua kaki dari hidung ke pangkal ekor, tinggal di lubang, berbulu cokelat kelabu, berkaki pendek tebal, berekor lebat, dan berkepala di antara anjing dan kucing.
claims.quote: Tarawhata himself in 1848 gave Mantell a description which is full of otter-like detail. It was, he said. two feet from nose to root of tail, lived in holes, had grislybrown fur, short thick legs. bushy tail and a head between that of a dog and cat.

claims.statement: The account added the interesting if puzzling information that there were two kinds, a water kind living on fish and a land kind living on lizards.
claims.statement_id: Laporan itu menambahkan keterangan yang menarik tetapi membingungkan bahwa ada dua jenis: jenis air yang hidup dari ikan dan jenis darat yang hidup dari kadal.
claims.quote: added the interesting if puzzling information that there were two kinds - a water kind living on fish. a land kind on lizards

claims.statement: Maopo held the tradition that the animal had been kept as a pet by his forefathers.
claims.statement_id: Maopo memegang tradisi bahwa hewan itu dahulu dipelihara oleh leluhurnya.
claims.quote: Maopo, who held the tradition of its having been kept as a pet by his forefathers

claims.statement: An angler fishing at dusk on the Waihopai River heard a splashing and something big swam up against the current to within two yards of him; he saw a small round head like a seal's.
claims.statement_id: Seorang pemancing di Sungai Waihopai saat senja mendengar percikan, lalu sesuatu yang besar berenang melawan arus hingga dua yard darinya; ia melihat kepala bulat kecil seperti kepala anjing laut.
claims.quote: while fishing at dusk on the Waihopai River a mile below Kennington he heard a splashing and something big swam up against the current to within two yards of him. Though fairly dark. it was close enough for him to see a small round head like a seal's.

claims.statement: Moffett, fishing in the Eglinton River in April 1924, saw a small dark animal running rather rapidly in a crouching manner; it had apparently come up out of the river and swiftly returned to it as he approached.
claims.statement_id: Moffett, saat memancing di Sungai Eglinton pada April 1924, melihat hewan kecil berwarna gelap berlari cepat dengan posisi merunduk; hewan itu tampaknya keluar dari sungai dan cepat kembali ke sana ketika ia mendekat.
claims.quote: G. l. Moffett in April 1924, while fishing in the Eglinton River. saw one morning, about 100 yards off, a small animal of a dark colour running rather rapidly in a crouching manner. It had apparently come up out of the river, to which it swiftly returned on Moffett's approach.

claims.statement: Pollock concludes that the waitoreke of Maori tradition is an actual, not a mythical, animal; that it is an otter (genus Lutra) of some Asian species yet to be identified; and that it was introduced centuries ago by storm-driven mariners or fishermen from South-east Asia.
claims.statement_id: Kesimpulan Pollock: waitoreke dalam tradisi Māori adalah hewan nyata, bukan mitos; ia berang-berang (otter) genus Lutra dari spesies Asia yang belum teridentifikasi; dan didatangkan berabad-abad lalu oleh pelaut atau nelayan yang terdampar badai dari Asia Tenggara.
claims.quote: (a) The waitoreke of Maori tradition is an actual, not a mythical, animal; (b) It is an otter (genus Lutra) of some Asian species yet to be identified; (c) It was introduced, probably about live centuries ago, by storm-driven mariners or fishermen from South-east Asia

claims.statement: Pollock suggests that, given the substitution of "k" for "ng" in South Island Maori dialects, the name could be the equivalent of "waitorengi", meaning "disappearing in the water".
claims.statement_id: Pollock mengusulkan bahwa dengan pergantian "k" menjadi "ng" dalam dialek Māori Pulau Selatan, nama itu bisa setara dengan "waitorengi" yang berarti "menghilang di dalam air".
claims.quote: Considering first the common substitution, in South Island Maori dialects, of 'k' for 'ng', it could be the equivalent of "waitorengi", meaning "disappearing iu the water".

claims.statement: According to Pollock, Maopo at Taumutu obviously lacked firsthand knowledge and seems to have become confused with the kaurehe, which is almost certainly the tuatara.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Pollock, Maopo di Taumutu jelas tidak punya pengetahuan langsung dan tampaknya keliru dengan kaurehe, yang hampir pasti adalah tuatara.
claims.quote: Maopo at Taumutu also obviously lacked firsthand knowledge, and seems to have become confused with the kaurehe, which is almost certainly the tuatara.

claims.statement: New Zealand's only recognised endemic land mammals are bats: the New Zealand lesser short-tailed bat and long-tailed bat.
claims.statement_id: Satu-satunya mamalia darat endemik Selandia Baru yang diakui adalah kelelawar: kelelawar ekor pendek kecil dan kelelawar ekor panjang Selandia Baru.
claims.quote: New Zealand's only recognised endemic land mammals are bats-New Zealand lesser short-tailed bat and New Zealand long-tailed bat.

claims.statement: The Yara-ma-yha-who is a legendary vampiric monster in Southeastern Australian Aboriginal lore.
claims.statement_id: Yara-ma-yha-who adalah monster pengisap darah dalam mitologi Aborigin tenggara Australia.
claims.quote: The Yara-ma-yha-who is a legendary vampiric monster found in Southeastern Australian Aboriginal mythology.

claims.statement: The Yara-ma-yha-who is said to dwell in fig trees.
claims.statement_id: Yara-ma-yha-who konon dikatakan bertempat tinggal di pepohonan ara.
claims.quote: The Yara-ma-yha-who is said to live in fig trees.

claims.statement: The legend is recounted by David Unaipon.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini dituturkan oleh David Unaipon.
claims.quote: The legend is recounted by David Unaipon.

claims.statement: Yara-ma-yha-who is a strange little red man about four feet high; the biggest parts of him are his head, mouth and stomach; he has no teeth, simply swallows his food, and can even swallow a grown man.
claims.statement_id: Yara-ma-yha-who adalah lelaki merah kecil yang tingginya sekitar empat kaki; bagian terbesarnya kepala, mulut, dan perut; mulutnya tak bergigi, ia menelan makanannya begitu saja, bahkan dapat menelan orang dewasa.
claims.quote: Yara-ma-yha-who A strange little red man who stands about four feet high. The biggest parts of him are his head, his mouth, and his stomach. He has no teeth in his mouth and simply swallows his food, and can even swallow a grown man.

claims.statement: His head is something like a snake's and he opens his mouth just as a snake does; the points of his fingers and the tips of his toes are cup-shaped, like the suckers of an octopus.
claims.statement_id: Kepalanya agak mirip kepala ular dan ia membuka mulut seperti ular; ujung jari tangan dan kakinya berbentuk cawan seperti pengisap gurita.
claims.quote: He has no teeth in his mouth and simply swallows his food, and can even swallow a grown man. His head is something like a snake's, and he open his mouth just as a snake does. The points of his fingers and the tips of his toes are cup-shaped, like the suckers of an octopus.

claims.statement: These creatures live mostly in thick, leafy trees and prefer the wild fig tree; they do not hunt but pounce upon a person, place their hands and feet upon the victim, and drain his blood.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk-makhluk ini sebagian besar tinggal di pohon rimbun dan lebih suka pohon ara liar; mereka tidak berburu, melainkan menerkam seseorang, menempelkan tangan dan kaki ke korban, dan menguras darahnya.
claims.quote: They live mostly in thick, leafy trees, and prefer the wild fig tree. They do not hunt for their food but simply pounce upon a person, and place their hands and feet upon the victim, draining his blood.

claims.statement: The Yara-ma-yha-who leaves enough blood to keep the victim alive while he walks round and gets an appetite; after returning he crawls like a goanna and sucks his prey into his mouth head first.
claims.statement_id: Yara-ma-yha-who tidak menyedot semua darah, melainkan menyisakan cukup untuk menjaga korban tetap hidup sementara ia berjalan-jalan mencari selera makan; setelah kembali ia merangkak seperti goanna dan menyedot korban ke mulutnya dengan kepala lebih dulu.
claims.quote: The Yara-ma-yha-who does not try to suck all the blood from the body, but leaves sufficient to keep the victim alive while he walks round and gets an appetite. After he returns, he lies down on the ground, facing the victim, and crawls like a goanna, and opens his mouth wide, and sucks his prey into his mouth head first.

claims.statement: He then stands and dances round until the prey is well inside his stomach, goes to a river or pool and drinks copious amounts of water, falls asleep, and on waking vomits the remains of his meal.
claims.statement_id: Ia lalu berdiri dan menari berkeliling sampai korban masuk jauh ke perutnya, pergi minum banyak air dari sungai atau kolam, tidur, dan setelah bangun memuntahkan sisa santapannya.
claims.quote: He then rises and stands on his little legs, and dances round until the prey is well inside his stomach. Then he goes to a river or pool of water and drinks copious amounts of water, before falling asleep. When he wakes he vomits the remains of his recent meal.

claims.statement: He checks several times whether his prey is feigning death by poking and tickling him; if there is no response and he goes to sleep, the victim can use the chance to run away.
claims.statement_id: Ia beberapa kali memeriksa apakah mangsanya pura-pura mati dengan menyodok dan menggelitiknya; bila tak ada reaksi dan ia tertidur, korban dapat memanfaatkan kesempatan itu untuk kabur.
claims.quote: He will check several times to see if his prey is not feigning death by poking him with a stick and tickling him. If he gets no response and goes to sleep, the victim can use the opportunity to run away.

claims.statement: Should the Yara-ma-yha-who fail to check his victim, the spirit of the wild fig tree would kill him by entering his head through his ear, causing a mumbling noise that ends in intense silence.
claims.statement_id: Jika Yara-ma-yha-who lalai memeriksa korbannya, roh pohon ara liar akan membunuhnya dengan masuk ke kepalanya lewat telinga, menimbulkan suara menggumam yang berakhir dalam keheningan total.
claims.quote: Should the Yara-ma-yha-who fail to check his victim, then the spirit of the wild fig tree would kill him by entering into his head through his ear, and causing a mumbling noise, ending with intense silence

claims.statement: A person caught and swallowed by one of the red men becomes shorter with each capture, until he at last resembles a Yara-ma-yha-who.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang tertangkap dan tertelan oleh salah satu lelaki merah itu menjadi semakin pendek setiap kali, hingga akhirnya menyerupai Yara-ma-yha-who.
claims.quote: A person who is caught and swallowed by one of the red men become shorter with each capture, until he at last resembles a Yara-ma-yha-who.

claims.statement: According to legend, the Yara-ma-yha-who is only active during the day and only targets living prey; "playing dead" until sunset is offered as a ploy to avoid attack.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, Yara-ma-yha-who hanya aktif pada siang hari dan hanya menyasar mangsa yang hidup; "pura-pura mati" sampai matahari terbenam disebut sebagai siasat untuk menghindari serangan.
claims.quote: According to legend, the Yara-ma-yha-who is only active during the day and only targets living prey. "Playing dead" until sunset is offered as a ploy to avoid attack.

claims.statement: Stories of this creature were reportedly told to misbehaving children.
claims.statement_id: Cerita tentang makhluk ini dilaporkan dituturkan kepada anak-anak yang nakal.
claims.quote: Stories of this creature were reportedly told to misbehaving children.

claims.statement: The creature's origin is believed to be the tarsier, and the story probably came to Australia with Malay settlers; the other theory is Thylacoleo carnifex, a carnivorous marsupial that dropped onto its prey from the tree tops.
claims.statement_id: Asal makhluk ini diyakini adalah tarsius, dan kemungkinan ceritanya dibawa ke Australia oleh pemukim Melayu; teori lain adalah Thylacoleo carnifex, marsupial karnivora yang menjatuhkan diri ke mangsa dari puncak pohon.
claims.quote: The origin of this creature is believed to be the tarsier; it is probable that the story was brought to Australia by Malay settlers. The other theory proposed is Thylacoleo carnifex, a carnivorous marsupial that dropped onto its prey from the tree tops

claims.statement: Instead of hunting, it is described as waiting for an unsuspecting traveller to rest under the tree, then dropping down and using its suckers to drain the victim's blood.
claims.statement_id: Alih-alih berburu, makhluk ini digambarkan menunggu pengelana yang tak curiga beristirahat di bawah pohon, lalu menjatuhkan diri dan memakai pengisapnya untuk menguras darah korban.
claims.quote: Instead of hunting for food, it is described as waiting for an unsuspecting traveller to rest under the tree. The creature then drops down and uses its suckers to drain the victim's blood.

claims.statement: In Polynesian languages aitu refers to ghosts or spirits, often malevolent.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa-bahasa Polinesia kata aitu merujuk pada hantu atau roh yang kerap bersifat jahat.
claims.quote: In Polynesian languages the word aitu refers to ghosts or spirits, often malevolent.

claims.statement: The word aitu is widespread across Western and Eastern Polynesia.
claims.statement_id: Kata aitu umum digunakan di banyak bahasa di Polinesia Barat dan Timur.
claims.quote: The word is common to many languages of Western and Eastern Polynesia.

claims.statement: In Tonga, ʻaitu or ʻeitu are lesser gods serving as patrons of villages and families.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Tonga ʻaitu atau ʻeitu adalah dewa-dewa pelindung desa dan keluarga.
claims.quote: In the mythology of Tonga, for example, ʻaitu or ʻeitu are lesser gods, many being patrons of specific villages and families.

claims.statement: In the Samoa Islands, aitu also means ghost.
claims.statement_id: Di Kepulauan Samoa, aitu juga berarti hantu.
claims.quote: In the Samoa Islands, aitu also means ghost.

claims.statement: In Māori mythology the word aitu refers to sickness, calamity or demons; the related word aituā means misfortune, accident, disaster.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Māori, kata aitu merujuk pada penyakit, bencana, atau iblis; kata terkait aituā berarti kemalangan, kecelakaan, dan malapetaka.
claims.quote: In Māori mythology, the word aitu refers to sickness, calamity, or demons; the related word aituā means misfortune, accident, disaster.

claims.statement: In Tahitian, aitu (syn. atua/raitu) can mean "god" or "spirit"; in other languages, including Rarotongan, Samoan, Sikaiana, Kapingamarangi, Takuu, Tuamotuan and Niuean, aitu are ghosts or spirits.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Tahiti, aitu (sinonim atua/raitu) dapat berarti "dewa" atau "roh"; dalam bahasa lain, termasuk Rarotonga, Samoa, Sikaiana, Kapingamarangi, Takuu, Tuamotu, dan Niue, aitu adalah hantu atau roh.
claims.quote: In Tahitian, aitu (syn. atua/raitu) can mean 'god' or 'spirit'; in other languages, including Rarotongan, Samoan, Sikaiana, Kapingamarangi, Takuu, Tuamotuan, and Niuean, aitu are ghosts or spirits.

claims.statement: In the Cook Islands Aitu is also the name of ancient tribes who came from the east; according to tradition some of the Aitu tribes settled on the islands of Aitutaki, Atiu and Mangaia.
claims.statement_id: Di Kepulauan Cook, Aitu juga nama suku-suku kuno yang datang dari timur; menurut tradisi, sebagian suku Aitu menetap di pulau Aitutaki, Atiu, dan Mangaia.
claims.quote: In Cook Islands Aitu is also the name of ancient tribes who came from the east. According to tradition, some of the Aitu tribes settled on the islands of Aitutaki, Atiu and Mangaia.

claims.statement: In other Austronesian cultures, cognates of aitu include the Micronesian aniti, Bunun hanitu, Filipino and Tao anito, and Malaysian and Indonesian hantu or antu.
claims.statement_id: Dalam budaya Austronesia lain, kerabat kata aitu mencakup aniti (Mikronesia), hanitu (Bunun), anito (Filipina dan Tao), serta hantu atau antu (Malaysia dan Indonesia).
claims.quote: In other Austronesian cultures, cognates of aitu include the Micronesian aniti, Bunun hanitu, Filipino and Tao anito, and Malaysian and Indonesian hantu or antu.

claims.statement: In the mythology of Tonga, ʻaitu or ʻeitu are lesser gods, many being patrons of specific villages and families; they often take the form of plants or animals, are often more cruel than other gods, and are regarded as having come from Samoa.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Tonga, ʻaitu atau ʻeitu adalah dewa-dewa rendah, banyak di antaranya pelindung desa dan keluarga tertentu; mereka sering berwujud tumbuhan atau hewan dan sering lebih kejam daripada dewa lain, serta dianggap berasal dari Samoa.
claims.quote: In the mythology of Tonga, for example, ʻaitu or ʻeitu are lesser gods, many being patrons of specific villages and families. They often take the form of plants or animals, and are often more cruel than other gods. These trouble-making gods are regarded as having come from Samoa.

claims.statement: At his birth a Samoan was supposed to be taken under the care of some god, or aitu, as it was called.
claims.statement_id: Saat lahir, seorang Samoa dianggap berada di bawah asuhan suatu dewa, atau aitu sebagaimana disebut.
claims.quote: At his birth a Samoan was supposed to be taken under the care of some god, or aitu, as it was called.

claims.statement: These gods were supposed to appear in some visible incarnation, and the particular thing in which his god was in the habit of appearing was to the Samoan an object of veneration.
claims.statement_id: Dewa-dewa ini dianggap tampil dalam suatu penjelmaan yang terlihat, dan benda tertentu tempat dewanya biasa tampil menjadi objek penghormatan bagi orang Samoa.
claims.quote: These gods were supposed to appear in some visible incarnation, and the particular thing in which his god was in the habit of appearing was to the Samoan an object of veneration.

claims.statement: One, for instance, saw his god in the eel, another in the shark, the turtle, the dog, the owl or the lizard, and so on throughout all the fish of the sea, birds, four-footed beasts and creeping things.
claims.statement_id: Misalnya, seseorang melihat dewanya pada belut, yang lain pada hiu, penyu, anjing, burung hantu, atau kadal, dan seterusnya pada semua ikan laut, burung, hewan berkaki empat, dan hewan melata.
claims.quote: One, for instance, saw his god in the eel, another in the shark, another in the turtle, another in the dog, another in the owl, another in the lizard, and so on throughout all the fish of the sea, and birds, and four-footed beasts, and creeping things.

claims.statement: A man would eat freely of the incarnation of another man's god, but would consider it death to injure or eat the incarnation of his own god; the god was supposed to avenge the insult by taking up his abode in that person's body.
claims.statement_id: Seseorang bebas memakan penjelmaan dewa orang lain, tetapi menganggap kematian bila melukai atau memakan penjelmaan dewanya sendiri; dewa itu dianggap membalas penghinaan dengan menetap di tubuh orang tersebut.
claims.quote: A man would eat freely of what was regarded as the incarnation of the god of another man, but the incarnation of his own particular god he would consider it death to injure or to eat. The god was supposed to avenge the insult by taking up his abode in that person's body

claims.statement: This class of genii, or tutelary deities, they called aitu fale, or gods of the house.
claims.statement_id: Golongan jin atau dewa pelindung ini mereka sebut aitu fale, atau dewa rumah.
claims.quote: This class of genii, or tutelary deities, they called aitu fale, or gods of the house.

claims.statement: Aitu Langi, or Gods of heaven: these gods were supposed to have fallen from the heavens at the call of a blind man to protect his son from a cannibal chief.
claims.statement_id: Aitu Langi, atau Dewa-dewa Langit: dewa-dewa ini dianggap jatuh dari langit atas panggilan seorang buta untuk melindungi putranya dari seorang kepala suku kanibal.
claims.quote: Aitu Langi, or Gods of heaven. 1. These gods were supposed to have fallen from the heavens at the call of a blind man to protect his son from a cannibal chief.

claims.statement: Bobbi-Bobbi was a supernatural being living in the heavens in Binbinga Dreamtime myths.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos suku Binbinga di Australia utara, Bobbi-Bobbi adalah makhluk gaib yang hidup di langit pada Masa Mimpi (Dreamtime).
claims.quote: In myths of the Binbinga people of northern Australia, Bobbi-Bobbi was a supernatural being who lived in the heavens in the Dreamtime.

claims.statement: He was a huge snake similar to the Rainbow Serpent, initially benevolent to humans.
claims.statement_id: Ia ular raksasa, mirip Ular Pelangi (Rainbow Serpent), dan pada mulanya baik hati kepada manusia.
claims.quote: He was a huge snake, similar to the Rainbow Serpent, and was originally benevolent towards humans.

claims.statement: From the heavens he saw that humans needed more than water to survive, so he created flying foxes for them to catch and eat.
claims.statement_id: Dari langit ia melihat manusia memerlukan lebih dari sekadar air untuk bertahan hidup, sehingga ia menciptakan kelelawar buah (flying fox) untuk mereka tangkap dan makan.
claims.quote: From the heavens, he saw that humans needed more than just water to survive, so he created flying foxes for them to catch and eat.

claims.statement: When the bats flew too high for the humans to catch, Bobbi-Bobbi removed one of his own ribs and gave it to humans, who used it as the first boomerang.
claims.statement_id: Ketika kelelawar terbang terlalu tinggi untuk ditangkap, Bobbi-Bobbi melepas salah satu tulang rusuknya dan memberikannya kepada manusia, yang memakainya sebagai bumerang pertama.
claims.quote: When the bats flew too high for the humans to catch them, Bobbi-Bobbi removed one of his own ribs and gave it to humans who used it as the first ever boomerang.

claims.statement: Two men pretended they wanted to open a hole in the sky and thank Bobbi-Bobbi personally; they hurled the rib-boomerang and tore a huge hole in the clouds, which startled Bobbi-Bobbi so much that he failed to catch it, and it fell back to Earth and killed the foolish men.
claims.statement_id: Dua lelaki berpura-pura ingin membuka lubang di langit untuk berterima kasih langsung kepada Bobbi-Bobbi; mereka melempar bumerang tulang rusuk itu dan merobek lubang besar di awan, sehingga Bobbi-Bobbi terkejut dan gagal menangkapnya, dan bumerang itu jatuh ke bumi serta membunuh kedua lelaki bodoh tersebut.
claims.quote: Two men pretended they wanted to open a hole in the sky and thank Bobbi-Bobbi personally. They hurled the rib-boomerang and tore a huge hole in the clouds which startled Bobbi-Bobbi so much that he failed to catch the boomerang which fell back to Earth and killed the foolish men.

claims.statement: This was the first time Death had visited the human race, so Bobbi-Bobbi has remained aloof in heaven ever since, making no more attempts to help humans.
claims.statement_id: Itulah pertama kalinya Kematian mengunjungi umat manusia, sehingga Bobbi-Bobbi sejak itu menjauh di surga dan tidak lagi berusaha menolong manusia.
claims.quote: This was the first time that Death had visited the human race, so Bobbi-Bobbi has remained aloof in heaven ever since, making no more attempts to help humans.

claims.statement: In the tale of the Snake Bobbi-Bobbi, two boys, a Paliarinji and a Tjamerum, were circumcised at Akuralla on the Macarthur River, in the country of the Binbinga tribe.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Ular Bobbi-Bobbi, dua anak laki-laki, seorang Paliarinji dan seorang Tjamerum, disunat di Akuralla di Sungai Macarthur, di wilayah suku Binbinga.
claims.quote: The Snake Bobbi-Bobbi Two boys, one a Paliarinji and the other a Tjamerum, were circumcised at Akuralla on the Macarthur River, in the country of the Binbinga tribe.

claims.statement: The snake Bobbi-bobbi heard the noise they made and sent a mob of Kinaquantj (flying foxes).
claims.statement_id: Ular Bobbi-bobbi mendengar bunyi yang mereka buat dan mengirim sekawanan Kinaquantj (kelelawar buah).
claims.quote: The snake Bobbi-bobbi heard the noise which they made, and sent a mob of Kinaquantj (flying foxes)

claims.statement: Just then the snake Bobbi-bobbi, who was underground watching them, took out one of his ribs and threw it on to a plain, where the Paliarinji boy found it and called it his boomerang.
claims.statement_id: Saat itu ular Bobbi-bobbi, yang berada di bawah tanah mengawasi mereka, mengambil salah satu tulang rusuknya dan melemparkannya ke dataran; anak Paliarinji menemukannya dan berkata bahwa itu bumerangnya.
claims.quote: Just then the snake Bobbi- bobbi, who was underground watching them, took out one of his ribs and threw it on to a plain, where the Paliarinji boy found it, and said, " Hullo, this is my boomerang,"

claims.statement: The Paliarinji boy threw it into the air and it flew straight up into the sky, making a great hole in the sky through which it disappeared out of sight.
claims.statement_id: Anak Paliarinji melemparnya ke udara dan bumerang itu melesat lurus ke langit, membuat lubang besar di langit sebelum lenyap dari pandangan.
claims.quote: Paliarinji threw it into the air, and it flew straight up into the sky, making a great hole in the latter, through which it disappeared out of sight.

claims.statement: Gradually they sank up to their knees, and then the snake caught hold of them and dragged them down, a big water-hole called Mumbi-mumbi arising at this spot.
claims.statement_id: Perlahan mereka tenggelam sampai lutut, lalu sang ular menangkap dan menyeret mereka ke bawah, dan sebuah lubang air besar bernama Mumbi-mumbi muncul di tempat itu.
claims.quote: Gradually they sank up to their knees, and then the snake caught hold of them and dragged them down, a big water-hole called Mumbi-mumbi arising at this spot.

claims.statement: The snake took the two boys down the Macarthur River and across to Waliangu Island, one of the Pellew group, and there they have remained ever since.
claims.statement_id: Sang ular membawa kedua anak itu menyusuri Sungai Macarthur dan menyeberang ke Pulau Waliangu, salah satu kelompok Pellew, dan mereka tinggal di sana sejak itu.
claims.quote: The snake took the twp^ boys away down the Macarthur River and across to Waliangu Island, one of the Pellew group, and there they have remained ever since.

claims.statement: At length they came to the Pellew Islands, some of which the snake made, telling Roumbaria that certain of them belonged to him and Urtalia that others belonged to him.
claims.statement_id: Akhirnya mereka tiba di Kepulauan Pellew, sebagian di antaranya dibuat oleh sang ular, yang menyatakan sebagian milik Roumbaria dan sebagian lain milik Urtalia.
claims.quote: At length they came to the Pellew Islands, some of which the snake made, telling Roumbaria that certain of them belonged to him, and Urtalia that others belonged to him.

claims.statement: At Aninjira Bobbi-bobbi was taken ill and threw out Urtalia, telling him that that country belonged to him.
claims.statement_id: Di Aninjira, Bobbi-bobbi jatuh sakit dan melepaskan Urtalia, dengan mengatakan bahwa negeri itu miliknya.
claims.quote: At Aninjira Bobbi-bobbi was taken ill and threw out the Urtalia, telling him that that country belonged to him.

claims.statement: Bobbi-bobbi is the name of an ancestral snake of the Anula tribe.
claims.statement_id: Bobbi-bobbi adalah nama seekor ular leluhur dari suku Anula.
claims.quote: Bobbi-bobbi - Name of an ancestral snake. Anula tribe.

claims.statement: Bobbi-bobbi is a snake in the Mara and Anula tribes.
claims.statement_id: Bobbi-bobbi adalah seekor ular dalam suku Mara dan Anula.
claims.quote: Bobbi-bobbi, a snake in the Mara and Anula tribes, 435

claims.statement: Spencer and Gillen write that ancestors such as the Bobbi-bobbi snake of the Anula and the Ulanji snake of the Binbinga are regarded as having been distinctly animals and not human beings.
claims.statement_id: Spencer dan Gillen menulis bahwa leluhur seperti ular Bobbi-bobbi dari Anula dan ular Ulanji dari Binbinga dianggap benar-benar hewan, bukan manusia.
claims.quote: The latter, - as, for example, in the case of the Wollunqua, the black snake and the deaf adder of the Warramunga, the Bobbi-bobbi snake of the Anula, and the Ulanji snake of the Binbinga, - are regarded as having been distinctly animals and not human beings.

claims.statement: The boomerang fell end on and stuck in the ground where the snake lay hidden, and he gripped and held on to it.
claims.statement_id: Bumerang itu jatuh dengan ujung lebih dulu dan tertancap di tanah tempat sang ular bersembunyi, lalu sang ular mencengkeram dan menahannya.
claims.quote: It fell end on and stuck in the ground where the snake lay hidden, and he gripped and held on to it.

claims.statement: The Anula, through whose country Bobbi-bobbi passed, have the following tradition with regard to them.
claims.statement_id: Suku Anula, yang wilayahnya dilewati Bobbi-bobbi, memiliki tradisi berikut tentang mereka.
claims.quote: The Anula, through whose country Bobbi-bobbi passed, have the following tradition with regard to them

claims.statement: Ikatere is a fish god and father of all sea creatures in Māori lore.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Māori dan Polinesia, Ikatere (juga ditulis Ika-tere, "ikan cepat") adalah dewa ikan, bapa semua makhluk laut, termasuk putri duyung.
claims.quote: In Māori and Polynesian mythology, Ikatere, also spelled Ika-tere, ('fast fish') is a fish god, the father of all sea creatures, including mermaids.

claims.statement: Ikatere is a son of Punga, grandson of Tangaroa, and brother of Tū-te-wehiwehi.
claims.statement_id: Ikatere adalah putra Punga, cucu Tangaroa, dan saudara Tū-te-wehiwehi.
claims.quote: He is a son of Punga, and a grandson of Tangaroa, and his brother is Tū-te-wehiwehi

claims.statement: Tangaroa had begotten Punga, and Punga had begotten two children, Ika-tere, the father of fish, and Tu-te-wehiwehi (or Tu-te-wanawana), the father of reptiles.
claims.statement_id: Tangaroa memperanakkan Punga, dan Punga memperanakkan dua anak, Ika-tere, bapa ikan, dan Tu-te-wehiwehi (atau Tu-te-wanawana), bapa reptil.
claims.quote: Tangaroa had begotten Punga, and ... he had begotten two children, Ika-tere, the father of fish, and Tu-te-wehiwehi, or Tu-te-wanawana, the father of reptiles.

claims.statement: When Tangaroa fled to the ocean, Tu-te-wehiwehi and Ika-tere and their children disputed how to escape the storms: Tu-te-wehiwehi and his party cried "Let us fly inland", but Ika-tere and his party cried "Let us fly to the sea".
claims.statement_id: Ketika Tangaroa melarikan diri ke samudra, Tu-te-wehiwehi dan Ika-tere beserta anak-anak mereka berselisih tentang cara lolos dari badai: Tu-te-wehiwehi dan kelompoknya berseru "Mari kita terbang ke daratan", tetapi Ika-tere dan kelompoknya berseru "Mari kita terbang ke laut".
claims.quote: When Tangaroa fled for safety to the ocean, then Tu-te-wehiwehi and Ika-tere, and their children, disputed together as to what they should do to escape from the storms, and Tu-te-wehiwehi and his party cried aloud, "Let us fly inland;" but Ika-tere and his party cried aloud, " Let us fly to the sea."

claims.statement: These two races of beings separated without delay: the fish fled in confusion to the sea, the reptiles sought safety in the forests and scrubs.
claims.statement_id: Kedua ras makhluk itu segera berpisah: ikan lari tunggang langgang ke laut, sedangkan reptil mencari selamat di hutan dan semak.
claims.quote: Then without delay these two races of beings separated. The fish fled in confusion to the sea, the reptiles sought safety in the forests and scrubs

claims.statement: Tu-te-wehiwehi shouted "Nay, nay, let us rather fly inland", and Ika-tere warned that the fate of him and his race would be that when caught, before being cooked, their scales would be singed off over a lighted wisp of dry fern.
claims.statement_id: Tu-te-wehiwehi menjawab "Tidak, tidak, lebih baik kita terbang ke daratan", lalu Ika-tere memperingatkan bahwa nasib dia dan rasnya kelak: saat ditangkap, sebelum dimasak, sisik mereka akan dihanguskan di atas seikat pakis kering yang dinyalakan.
claims.quote: But Tu-te-wehiwehi shouted in answer, ' Nay, nay, let us rather fly inland.' " Then Ika-tere warned him, saying, ' Fly ... then ; and the fate of you and your race will be, that when they catch you, before you are cooked, they will singe off your scales over a lighted wisp of dry fern.

claims.statement: Tu-te-wehiwehi answered "Seek safety, then, in the sea" and foretold the future fate of that race: to be laid upon the top of the cooked vegetable food, when little baskets are served out to each person, to give it a relish.
claims.statement_id: Tu-te-wehiwehi menjawab "Carilah selamat di laut, kalau begitu", dan meramalkan nasib kelak ras itu: diletakkan di atas makanan nabati yang dimasak, ketika keranjang kecil dibagikan kepada tiap orang, untuk memberi cita rasa.
claims.quote: But Tu-te-wehiwehi answered him, saying, ' Seek safety, then, in the sea ; and the future fate of your race will be, that when they serve out little baskets of cooked vegetable food to each person, you will be laid upon the top of the food to give a relish to it.

claims.statement: Ikatere chose to keep his children, the fish, in the sea, while Tū-te-wehiwehi chose to take his children, reptiles, to the land.
claims.statement_id: Ikatere memilih menjaga anak-anaknya, ikan, di laut, sedangkan Tū-te-wehiwehi memilih membawa anak-anaknya, reptil, ke darat.
claims.quote: Ikatere chose to keep his children, the fish, to the sea, while Tū-te-wehiwehi chose to take his children, reptiles, to the land.

claims.statement: A saying that refers to these choices runs "Tāua ki uta, tāua ki te wai" ("We of the land, we of the sea").
claims.statement_id: Pepatah yang merujuk pilihan itu berbunyi "Tāua ki uta, tāua ki te wai" ("Kita di darat, kita di laut").
claims.quote: Tāua ki uta, tāua ki te wai. We of the land, we of the sea.

claims.statement: When Tāwhirimātea (god of storms) made war against his brothers over the separation of Rangi and Papa (sky and earth), Ikatere and Tū-te-wehiwehi were among those who had to flee from his wrath to survive.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Tāwhirimātea (dewa badai) berperang melawan saudara-saudaranya karena pemisahan Rangi dan Papa (langit dan bumi), Ikatere dan Tū-te-wehiwehi termasuk yang harus lari dari amarahnya demi bertahan hidup.
claims.quote: When Tāwhirimātea (god of storms) made war against his brothers for the separation of Rangi and Papa (sky and earth), Ikatere and Tū-te-wehiwehi were among those who had to flee from his wrath for their survival.

claims.statement: Nāmaka appears as a sea goddess in the Pele family in Hawaiian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Nāmaka adalah dewi laut dalam keluarga Pele dalam mitologi Hawaii.
claims.quote: In Hawaiian mythology, Nāmaka (or Nā-maka-o-Kahaʻi, the eyes of Kahaʻi) appears as a sea goddess in the Pele family.

claims.statement: Nāmaka is the older sister of Pele-honua-mea.
claims.statement_id: Nāmaka adalah kakak perempuan dari Pele-honua-mea.
claims.quote: She is an older sister of Pele-honua-mea.

claims.statement: She is the daughter of Ku-waha-ilo and Haumea, whose other children are Pele, the Hiʻiaka sisters, the Kama brothers, and the bird Halulu.
claims.statement_id: Ia putri Ku-waha-ilo dan Haumea, yang anak-anak lainnya adalah Pele, saudari-saudari Hiʻiaka, saudara-saudara Kama, dan burung Halulu.
claims.quote: She is the daughter of Ku-waha-ilo and Haumea, whose other children are Pele, the Hiʻiaka sisters, the Kama brothers, and the bird Halulu.

claims.statement: When Pele quarrels with her powerful sister Nāmaka, Nāmaka sends tidal waves to destroy Pele's lands and homes; Pele, helped by her family, fights Nāmaka but is defeated.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Pele bertengkar dengan saudarinya yang perkasa, Nāmaka, Nāmaka mengirim gelombang pasang untuk menghancurkan tanah dan rumah Pele; Pele yang dibantu keluarganya melawan Nāmaka, tetapi dikalahkan.
claims.quote: When Pele quarrels with her powerful sister Nāmaka, Nāmaka sends tidal waves to destroy Pele's lands and homes. Helped by her family, Pele fights Nāmaka, but Nāmaka defeats her.

claims.statement: In Thrum's Kane-huna-moku myth, Nāmaka is called the chiefess of the Mu and Menehune people when they are summoned to build the watercourse for Kikiaola at Waimea on Kauaʻi.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos Kane-huna-moku dari Thrum, Nāmaka disebut kepala perempuan orang Mu dan Menehune ketika mereka dipanggil membangun saluran air Kikiaola di Waimea, Kauaʻi.
claims.quote: In Thrum's Kane-huna-moku myth, Nāmaka is called the chiefess of the Mu and Menehune people when they are summoned to build the watercourse for Kikiaola at Waimea on Kauaʻi.

claims.statement: When Pele causes a conflagration by staying too close to the fire god Lono-makua, Nāmaka drives her away; another legend says Nāmaka's guardian dog Moela is reduced to ashes when he touches ʻAukele.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Pele menyebabkan kebakaran besar karena terlalu dekat dengan dewa api Lono-makua, Nāmaka mengusirnya; legenda lain menyebut anjing penjaga Nāmaka, Moela, menjadi abu ketika menyentuh ʻAukele.
claims.quote: When Pele causes a conflagration by staying too close to the fire god Lono-makua, Nāmaka drives her away. Another legend mentions that Nāmaka's guardian dog, Moela is reduced to ashes when he touches ʻAukele.

claims.statement: Another version states that Pele was born from the head of Haumea, while Nāmaka was born from her thighs.
claims.statement_id: Versi lain menyatakan Pele lahir dari kepala Haumea, sedangkan Nāmaka lahir dari pahanya.
claims.quote: Another version states that Pele was born from the head of Haumea, while Nāmaka was born from her thighs

claims.statement: The god Ku, under the name Ku-waha-ilo, was the father and Haumea the mother; two daughters were born, the first, Na-maka-o-ka-hai, from the breasts of Haumea, and Pele from the thighs.
claims.statement_id: Dewa Ku, dengan nama Ku-waha-ilo, adalah bapa dan Haumea ibu; dua putri lahir, yang pertama, Na-maka-o-ka-hai, lahir dari dada Haumea dan Pele dari pahanya.
claims.quote: The god Ku, under the name Ku-waha-ilo, was the father. Haumea was the mother. ... Two daughters were born. The first, Na-maka-o-ka-hai, was born from the breasts of Haumea. Pele was born from the thighs.

claims.statement: Na-maka-o-ka-hai, a sea-goddess, became Pele's most bitter enemy as a result of family trouble, fighting her with floods of water, according to the legends; the original household thus represented the two eternal enemies, fire and water.
claims.statement_id: Na-maka-o-ka-hai, dewi laut, karena perselisihan keluarga menjadi musuh terpahit Pele dan melawannya dengan banjir air, menurut legenda; rumah tangga asal itu mewakili dua musuh abadi, api dan air.
claims.quote: Na-maka-o-ka-hai, a sea-goddess, as a result of family trouble, became Pele's most bitter enemy, fighting her with floods of water, according to the legends. Thus the original household represented the two eternal enemies, fire and water.

claims.statement: Pele's brother Ka-moho-alii and her older sister Na-maka-o-ka-hai belonged to the powers of the sea.
claims.statement_id: Saudara Pele, Ka-moho-alii, dan kakak perempuannya, Na-maka-o-ka-hai, termasuk kekuatan laut.
claims.quote: Pele's brother, Ka-moho-alii, and her older sister, Na-maka-o-ka-hai, however, belonged to the powers of the sea.

claims.statement: High tides and floods from the seas destroyed Pele's home and lands; Ka-moho-alii, the shark-god and Pele's elder brother, called the whole family to aid Pele, but Na-maka-o-ka-hai fought and defeated them all, broke down their houses and drove them into the ocean.
claims.statement_id: Pasang tinggi dan banjir dari laut menghancurkan rumah dan tanah Pele; Ka-moho-alii, dewa hiu dan kakak Pele, memanggil seluruh keluarga membantu Pele, tetapi Na-maka-o-ka-hai melawan dan mengalahkan mereka semua, merobohkan rumah mereka dan mengusir mereka ke samudra.
claims.quote: High tides and floods from the seas destroyed Pele's home and lands. Then the elder brother of Pele-Ka-moho-alii, the shark-god-called for all the family to aid Pele. Na-maka-o-ka-hai fought the whole family and defeated them. She broke down their houses and drove them into the ocean.

claims.statement: Na-maka-o-ka-hai went to the highest of all the mythical lands of the ancestors, Nuu-mea-lani ("the raised dais of heaven"), from where she could look over all the seas from Ka-la-kee-nui-a-Kane to Kauai.
claims.statement_id: Na-maka-o-ka-hai pergi ke negeri leluhur mitos yang tertinggi, Nuu-mea-lani ("mimbar tinggi surga"), tempat ia dapat menatap seluruh laut dari Ka-la-kee-nui-a-Kane sampai Kauai.
claims.quote: Na-maka-o-ka-hai went to the highest of all the mythical lands of the ancestors, Nuu-mea-lani (The raised dais of heaven). There she could look over all the seas from Ka-la-kee-nui-a-Kane to Kauai

claims.statement: The two sisters fought hand to hand for a long time along the western slope of the mountain Hale-a-ka-la; Na-maka-o-ka-hai tore the body of Pele and broke her lava bones into great pieces which lie to this day along the seacoast of the district called Kahiki-nui.
claims.statement_id: Kedua saudari itu bertarung tangan kosong lama di lereng barat gunung Hale-a-ka-la; Na-maka-o-ka-hai mencabik tubuh Pele dan mematahkan tulang lavanya menjadi bongkahan besar yang hingga kini terletak di pesisir distrik Kahiki-nui.
claims.quote: The battle was fought by the two sisters hand to hand. The conflict lasted for a long time along the western slope of the mountain Hale-a-ka-la. Na-maka-o-ka-hai tore the body of Pele and broke her lava bones into great pieces which lie to this day along the seacoast of the district called Kahiki-nui.

claims.statement: Na-maka-o-ka-hai went off toward Nuu-mea-lani rejoicing in the destruction of her hated enemy, and passed on there knowing that she could never again overcome the spirit of Pele, the goddess of fire.
claims.statement_id: Na-maka-o-ka-hai menuju Nuu-mea-lani dengan gembira atas kehancuran musuh yang dibencinya, dan ia terus ke sana karena tahu tidak akan pernah lagi dapat mengalahkan roh Pele, dewi api.
claims.quote: Na-maka-o-ka-hai went off toward Nuu-mea-lani rejoicing in the destruction of her hated enemy. ... She passed on to Nuu-mea-lani, knowing that she could never again overcome the spirit of Pele, the goddess of fire.

claims.statement: In this story Pele's angry sister Na-maka-o-ka-hai had driven her from the island Kauai.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah ini, Na-maka-o-ka-hai, saudari Pele yang murka, pernah mengusir Pele dari pulau Kauai.
claims.quote: Many, many years after Pele's angry sister Na-maka-o-ka-hai had driven her from the island Kauai

claims.statement: A greater sorcerer married Na-maka-o-ka-hai; after a time he saw Pele and her beautiful young sister Hiiaka and secretly took them to be his wives; this sorcerer was Au-kele-nui-a-iku.
claims.statement_id: Seorang penyihir yang lebih besar menikahi Na-maka-o-ka-hai; setelah beberapa waktu ia melihat Pele dan adik bungsunya yang cantik, Hiiaka, dan diam-diam mengambil mereka sebagai istri; penyihir itu adalah Au-kele-nui-a-iku.
claims.quote: A greater sorcerer married Na-maka-o-ka-hai. After a time he saw Pele and her beautiful young sister Hiiaka. He took them secretly to be his wives. This sorcerer was Au-kele-nui-a-iku.

claims.statement: Namaka is the name of the smaller and inner moon of the dwarf planet Haumea, and its other moon is named after Namaka's sister, Hiʻiaka.
claims.statement_id: Namaka adalah nama bulan yang lebih kecil dan lebih dalam dari planet kerdil Haumea, dan bulan lainnya dinamai menurut saudari Namaka, Hiʻiaka.
claims.quote: Namaka is the name of the smaller and inner moon of the dwarf planet Haumea, and its other moon is named after Namaka's sister, Hiʻiaka.

claims.statement: Nāmaka took ʻAukelenuiaʻīkū, who had arrived in Lalakeenuiakane or in Kahiki (Tahiti), as her husband, but he later became the husband of her sister Pele.
claims.statement_id: Nāmaka mengambil ʻAukelenuiaʻīkū, yang datang dari Lalakeenuiakane atau Kahiki (Tahiti), sebagai suaminya, tetapi ia kemudian menjadi suami saudarinya, Pele.
claims.quote: Nāmaka took ʻAukelenuiaʻīkū as her husband, who had arrived in Lalakeenuiakane or in Kahiki (Tahiti), but he later became the husband of her sister Pele

claims.statement: Punga is the ancestor of sharks, lizards, and rays in Māori mythology.
claims.statement_id: Punga adalah makhluk gaib leluhur ikan hiu, kadal, dan pari dalam mitologi Māori.
claims.quote: In Māori mythology, Punga is a supernatural being, the ancestor of sharks, lizards, rays, and all deformed, ugly things.

claims.statement: All strange animals are Punga's children, giving rise to the saying Te aitanga a Punga.
claims.statement_id: Hewan-hewan aneh dianggap keturunan Punga, memunculkan peribahasa Te aitanga a Punga.
claims.quote: All ugly and strange animals are Punga's children. Hence the saying Te aitanga a Punga (the offspring of Punga) used to describe an ugly person.

claims.statement: Punga is a son of Tangaroa, the god of the sea; when Tāwhirimātea (god of storms) made war against his brothers after Rangi and Papa were separated, Punga's two sons, Ikatere and Tū-te-wehiwehi, had to flee for their lives.
claims.statement_id: Punga adalah putra Tangaroa, dewa laut; ketika Tāwhirimātea (dewa badai) berperang melawan saudara-saudaranya setelah Rangi dan Papa dipisahkan, kedua putra Punga, Ikatere dan Tū-te-wehiwehi, harus lari menyelamatkan diri.
claims.quote: Punga is a son of Tangaroa, the god of the sea, and when Tāwhirimātea (god of storms) made war against his brothers after they separated Rangi and Papa (sky and earth), the two sons of Punga, Ikatere and Tū-te-wehiwehi, had to flee for their lives.

claims.statement: Ikatere fled to the sea and became the ancestor of certain fish, while Tū-te-wehiwehi took refuge in the forest and became the ancestor of lizards.
claims.statement_id: Ikatere lari ke laut dan menjadi leluhur ikan tertentu, sedangkan Tū-te-wehiwehi berlindung di hutan dan menjadi leluhur kadal.
claims.quote: Ikatere fled to the sea, and became the ancestor of certain fish, while Tū-te-wehiwehi took refuge in the forest, and became the ancestor of lizards.

claims.statement: Punga's name has a maritime origin: in Māori "punga" means "anchor stone", and in tropical Polynesia related words refer to coral stone, also used as an anchor.
claims.statement_id: Nama Punga berasal dari dunia bahari: dalam bahasa Māori "punga" berarti "batu jangkar", dan di Polinesia tropis kata-kata terkait merujuk pada batu karang yang juga dipakai sebagai jangkar.
claims.quote: As is appropriate for a son of Tangaroa, Punga's name has a maritime origin - in the Māori language, 'punga' means 'anchor stone' - in tropical Polynesia, related words refer to coral stone, also used as an anchor

claims.statement: According to some versions, Punga is the son of Rangi-potiki (father sky) and Papatūānuku (mother earth) and a twin brother to Here.
claims.statement_id: Menurut beberapa versi, Punga adalah putra Rangi-potiki (bapa langit) dan Papatūānuku (ibu bumi) serta saudara kembar Here.
claims.quote: According to some versions, Punga is the son of Rangi-potiki (father sky) and Papatūānuku (mother earth) and a twin brother to Here.

claims.statement: In a version of the Tāwhaki epic that White attributes to the Ngāti Hau tribe, Punga is named as a brother of Karihi and Hemā; in many versions, however, he is a cousin of the brothers Karihi and Tāwhaki.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi epos Tāwhaki yang oleh White dikaitkan dengan suku Ngāti Hau, Punga disebut saudara Karihi dan Hemā; tetapi dalam banyak versi ia sepupu kakak-beradik Karihi dan Tāwhaki.
claims.quote: In a version of the epic of Tāwhaki attributed by White to the Ngāti Hau tribe, Punga is named as a brother of Karihi and Hemā; however, in many versions, he is a cousin of the brothers Karihi and Tāwhaki

claims.statement: In some Hawaiian stories, Hema and Punga are sons of Aikanaka and Hinahanaiakamalama.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa kisah Hawaii, Hema dan Punga adalah putra Aikanaka dan Hinahanaiakamalama.
claims.quote: In some Hawaiian stories, Hema and Punga are sons of Aikanaka and Hinahanaiakamalama

claims.statement: Tangaroa had begotten Punga, and Punga had begotten two children, Ika-tere, the father of fish, and Tu-te-wehiwehi (or Tu-te-wanawana), the father of reptiles.
claims.statement_id: Tangaroa memperanakkan Punga, dan Punga memperanakkan dua anak, Ika-tere, bapa ikan, dan Tu-te-wehiwehi (atau Tu-te-wanawana), bapa reptil.
claims.quote: Tangaroa had begotten Punga, and ... he had begotten two children, Ika-tere, the father of fish, and Tu-te-wehiwehi, or Tu-te-wanawana, the father of reptiles.

claims.statement: The party of Punga rushed to the sea.
claims.statement_id: Kelompok Punga bergegas ke laut.
claims.quote: the party of Punga rushed to the sea.

claims.statement: Rangi-potiki's second wife was Papatuanuku, who gave birth to Rehua (a star), Rongo, Tangaroa, Tahu, and Punga and Here, twins.
claims.statement_id: Istri kedua Rangi-potiki adalah Papatuanuku, yang melahirkan anak-anak berikut: Rehua (sebuah bintang), Rongo, Tangaroa, Tahu, serta Punga dan Here yang kembar.
claims.quote: Rangi-potiki's second wife was Papatuanuku. She gave birth to the following children:- Rehua (a star). Rongo. Tangaroa. Tahu. Punga and Here, twins.

claims.statement: Punga was the ancestor of the lizard, shark and ill-favoured creatures; hence the proverb "aitanga-a-Punga" (child of Punga) to denote an ugly fellow.
claims.statement_id: Punga adalah leluhur kadal, hiu, dan makhluk berwajah buruk; karena itu ada peribahasa "aitanga-a-Punga" (anak Punga) untuk menyebut orang yang buruk rupa.
claims.quote: Punga was ancestor of the lizard, shark, and ill-favoured creatures: hence the proverb "aitanga-a-Punga" (=child of Punga) to denote an ugly fellow.

claims.statement: Taniwha are large supernatural beings living in deep river pools, caves, or seas with dangerous currents.
claims.statement_id: Taniwha adalah makhluk gaib besar yang hidup di lubuk sungai dalam, gua, atau laut berarus kuat.
claims.quote: In Māori mythology, taniwha ... are large supernatural beings that live in deep pools in rivers, dark caves, or in the sea, especially in places with dangerous currents or deceptive breakers (giant waves).

claims.statement: Taniwha are respected as kaitiaki protective guardians of people and places.
claims.statement_id: Taniwha dihormati sebagai kaitiaki penjaga pelindung manusia dan tempat.
claims.quote: They may be considered highly respected kaitiaki (protective guardians) of people and places, or in some traditions as dangerous, predatory beings

claims.statement: Linguists have reconstructed taniwha to Proto-Oceanic *tanifa meaning "shark species"; in Tongan and Niuean tenifa refers to a large dangerous shark, as does Samoan tanifa, while Tokelauan tanifa is a sea-monster that eats people.
claims.statement_id: Para ahli bahasa merekonstruksi kata taniwha ke bahasa Proto-Oseanik *tanifa yang berarti "spesies hiu"; dalam bahasa Tonga dan Niue tenifa berarti hiu besar berbahaya, demikian pula tanifa Samoa, sedangkan tanifa Tokelau adalah monster laut pemakan manusia.
claims.quote: Linguists have reconstructed the word taniwha to Proto-Oceanic *tanifa, with the meaning "shark species". In Tongan and Niuean, tenifa refers to a large dangerous shark, as does the Samoan tanifa; the Tokelauan tanifa is a sea-monster that eats people.

claims.statement: At sea, a taniwha often appears as a whale or a large shark such as a southern right whale or whale shark; compare the Māori name for the great white shark, mangō-taniwha.
claims.statement_id: Di laut, taniwha sering tampak sebagai paus atau hiu besar seperti paus sikat selatan atau hiu paus; bandingkan nama Māori untuk hiu putih besar, mangō-taniwha.
claims.quote: At sea, a taniwha often appears as a whale or a large shark such as southern right whale or whale shark; compare the Māori name for the great white shark: mangō-taniwha.

claims.statement: In inland waters they may still be of whale-like dimensions but look more like a gecko or tuatara with a row of spines along the back; other taniwha appear as a floating log that behaves disconcertingly, and some can tunnel through the earth, uprooting trees.
claims.statement_id: Di perairan pedalaman, mereka mungkin tetap berukuran sebesar paus tetapi tampak lebih mirip cicak atau tuatara dengan deretan duri di punggung; taniwha lain tampak sebagai batang kayu apung yang bertingkah mengganggu, dan sebagian dapat menerobos tanah sambil mencabut pohon.
claims.quote: In inland waters, they may still be of whale-like dimensions, but look more like a gecko or a tuatara, having a row of spines along the back. Other taniwha appear as a floating log, which behaves in a disconcerting way. Some can tunnel through the earth, uprooting trees in the process.

claims.statement: Legends credit certain taniwha with creating harbours by carving a channel to the ocean; Wellington's harbour, Te Whanganui-a-Tara, was reputedly carved out by two taniwha.
claims.statement_id: Legenda menganggap taniwha tertentu menciptakan pelabuhan dengan memahat saluran ke samudra; pelabuhan Wellington, Te Whanganui-a-Tara, konon dipahat oleh dua taniwha.
claims.quote: Legends credit certain taniwha with creating harbours by carving out a channel to the ocean. Wellington's harbour, Te Whanganui-a-Tara, was reputedly carved out by two taniwha.

claims.statement: Lake Waikaremoana in the Te Urewera Ranges area of Wairoa District was also reputedly carved out by taniwha; other taniwha allegedly caused landslides beside lakes or rivers.
claims.statement_id: Danau Waikaremoana di kawasan Pegunungan Te Urewera, Distrik Wairoa, juga konon dipahat oleh taniwha; taniwha lain disebut menyebabkan tanah longsor di tepi danau atau sungai.
claims.quote: Lake Waikaremoana in Te Urewera Ranges area of Wairoa District was also reputedly carved out by taniwha. Other taniwha allegedly caused landslides beside lakes or rivers.

claims.statement: Taniwha can be male or female; Āraiteuru is said to have arrived in New Zealand with the early voyaging canoes and her eleven sons are credited with creating the various branches of the Hokianga Harbour.
claims.statement_id: Taniwha dapat jantan atau betina; Āraiteuru konon tiba di Selandia Baru bersama kano-kano pelayaran awal, dan kesebelas putranya dianggap menciptakan berbagai cabang Pelabuhan Hokianga.
claims.quote: Taniwha can either be male or female. The taniwha Āraiteuru is said to have arrived in New Zealand with the early voyaging canoes and her eleven sons are credited with creating the various branches of the Hokianga Harbour.
