claims.statement: Many well-known taniwha arrived from Hawaiki, often as guardians of a particular ancestral canoe; once in Aotearoa they took on a protective role over the descendants of the crew of the canoe they had accompanied.
claims.statement_id: Banyak taniwha terkenal tiba dari Hawaiki, sering sebagai penjaga kano leluhur tertentu; setelah tiba di Aotearoa, mereka berperan melindungi keturunan awak kano yang mereka dampingi.
claims.quote: Many well-known taniwha arrived from Hawaiki, often as guardians of a particular ancestral canoe. Once arrived in Aotearoa, they took on a protective role over the descendants of the crew of the canoe they had accompanied.

claims.statement: When accorded appropriate respect, taniwha usually acted well towards their people; they guarded by warning of the approach of enemies through a priest who was a medium, and sometimes saved people from drowning.
claims.statement_id: Bila dihormati sepantasnya, taniwha biasanya bersikap baik kepada umatnya; mereka menjaga dengan memperingatkan datangnya musuh lewat seorang imam yang menjadi medium, dan kadang menyelamatkan orang dari tenggelam.
claims.quote: When accorded appropriate respect, taniwha usually acted well towards their people. Taniwha acted as guardians by warning of the approach of enemies, communicating the information via a priest who was a medium; sometimes the taniwha saved people from drowning.

claims.statement: Because they lived in dangerous or dark and gloomy places, people were careful to placate the taniwha with appropriate offerings when they needed to be near or pass its lair; the offering was often a green twig with a fitting incantation.
claims.statement_id: Karena mereka tinggal di tempat berbahaya atau gelap dan suram, orang berhati-hati menenangkan taniwha dengan persembahan yang pantas bila harus berada di dekat atau melewati sarangnya; persembahan itu sering berupa ranting hijau disertai mantra.
claims.quote: Because they lived in dangerous or dark and gloomy places, the people were careful to placate the taniwha with appropriate offerings if they needed to be in the vicinity or to pass by its lair. These offerings were often of a green twig, accompanied by a fitting incantation.

claims.statement: In their role as guardians, taniwha were vigilant that people respected the restrictions of tapu and made certain violations were punished; taniwha were especially dangerous to people from other tribes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam peran penjaga, taniwha waspada agar orang menghormati larangan tapu dan memastikan setiap pelanggaran tapu dihukum; taniwha terutama berbahaya bagi orang dari suku lain.
claims.quote: In their role as guardians, taniwha were vigilant to ensure that the people respected the restrictions imposed by tapu. They made certain that any violations of tapu were punished. Taniwha were especially dangerous to people from other tribes.

claims.statement: There are many legends of battles with taniwha, on land and at sea, often soon after the settlement of New Zealand and generally after a taniwha had attacked and eaten a person from a tribe it had no connection with; the humans always manage to outwit and defeat the taniwha.
claims.statement_id: Ada banyak legenda pertempuran melawan taniwha di darat dan laut, sering terjadi tak lama setelah permukiman Selandia Baru, biasanya setelah taniwha menyerang dan memakan orang dari suku yang tak berhubungan dengannya; manusia selalu berhasil mengakali dan mengalahkannya.
claims.quote: There are many legends of battles with taniwha, both on land and at sea. Often these conflicts took place soon after the settlement of New Zealand, generally after a taniwha had attacked and eaten a person from a tribe that it had no connection with. Always, the humans manage to outwit and defeat the taniwha.

claims.statement: When Hotu-puku, a taniwha of the Rotorua district, was killed, his stomach was cut open to reveal a number of bodies of men, women and children, whole and undigested, as well as various body parts.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Hotu-puku, taniwha di distrik Rotorua, dibunuh, perutnya dibelah dan memperlihatkan sejumlah jasad pria, wanita, dan anak-anak yang masih utuh dan belum tercerna, serta berbagai potongan tubuh.
claims.quote: When Hotu-puku, a taniwha of the Rotorua district, was killed, his stomach was cut open to reveal a number of bodies of men, women, and children, whole and still undigested, as well as various body parts.

claims.statement: Ngārara Huarau is a taniwha known from the myths of several groups of Māori in the northern South Island; in most versions the monster eats several villagers and captures a young woman whom he keeps in a cave by the sea.
claims.statement_id: Ngārara Huarau adalah taniwha yang dikenal dari mitos beberapa kelompok Māori di bagian utara Pulau Selatan; dalam kebanyakan versi, monster itu memakan beberapa penduduk desa dan menawan seorang perempuan muda di sebuah gua tepi laut.
claims.quote: Ngārara Huarau is a taniwha known from the myths of several groups of Māori in the northern South Island. In most versions of the story, the monster eats several villagers and captures a young woman whom he keeps in a cave by the sea.

claims.statement: Tāmure lived at Hauraki and was understood to have a magical mere/pounamu with powers to defeat taniwha.
claims.statement_id: Tāmure tinggal di Hauraki dan dipahami memiliki mere/pounamu ajaib yang berkuasa mengalahkan taniwha.
claims.quote: Tāmure lived at Hauraki and was understood to have a magical mere/pounamu with powers to defeat taniwha.

claims.statement: Sometimes a person who had dealings with taniwha during their lifetime might turn into a taniwha after they died.
claims.statement_id: Kadang orang yang berurusan dengan taniwha semasa hidup dapat menjadi taniwha setelah meninggal.
claims.quote: Sometimes, a person who had dealings with taniwha during their lifetime might turn into a taniwha after they died.

claims.statement: Arising from the role of taniwha as tribal guardians, the word can also refer in a complimentary way to chiefs.
claims.statement_id: Berasal dari peran taniwha sebagai penjaga suku, kata itu juga dapat menyebut kepala suku dengan nada memuji.
claims.quote: Arising from the role of taniwha as tribal guardians, the word can also refer in a complimentary way to chiefs.

claims.statement: In recent years taniwha have featured prominently in New Zealand news broadcasts because taniwha spirits have been referenced in court cases and legal negotiations.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa tahun terakhir, taniwha tampil menonjol dalam siaran berita Selandia Baru karena roh taniwha disebut dalam perkara pengadilan dan berbagai perundingan hukum.
claims.quote: "In more recent years, taniwha have featured prominently in New Zealand news broadcasts-due to taniwha spirits being referenced in both court cases and in various legal negotiations."

claims.statement: In 2002 Ngāti Naho, a Māori iwi from the Meremere district, successfully ensured that part of State Highway 1 was rerouted to protect the abode of their legendary protector.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2002, Ngāti Naho, iwi Māori dari distrik Meremere, berhasil membuat sebagian jalan raya utama, State Highway 1, dialihkan demi melindungi tempat tinggal pelindung legendaris mereka.
claims.quote: In 2002, Ngāti Naho, a Māori iwi (tribe) from the Meremere district, successfully ensured that part of the country's major highway, State Highway 1, be rerouted in order to protect the abode of their legendary protector.

claims.statement: The Māori academic Ranginui Walker said that in the modern age a taniwha was the manifestation of a coping mechanism for some Māori; it did not mean a creature was actually lurking in the water, only a way of indicating they were troubled by some incident or event.
claims.statement_id: Akademisi Māori Ranginui Walker mengatakan bahwa di zaman modern taniwha adalah perwujudan mekanisme penanggulangan bagi sebagian orang Māori; itu tidak berarti ada makhluk yang mengintai di air, melainkan cara menyatakan bahwa mereka resah oleh suatu peristiwa.
claims.quote: Māori academic Ranginui Walker said that in the modern age a taniwha was the manifestation of a coping mechanism for some Māori. It did not mean there actually was a creature lurking in the water, it was just their way of indicating they were troubled by some incident or event.

claims.statement: Moʻo or Moho, reptilian deities in Hawaiian lore, strongly share characteristics with taniwha as being both protector and harmful to men, shape-shifting and so on.
claims.statement_id: Moʻo atau Moho, dewa reptil dalam tradisi Hawaii, sangat mirip taniwha karena sama-sama pelindung sekaligus berbahaya bagi manusia, dan dapat berubah wujud.
claims.quote: Moʻo or Moho, reptilian deities which can be seen in Hawaiian lore, strongly share characteristics with Taniwha as being both protector and harmful to men, shape-shifting, and so on.

claims.statement: In this story a parrot-feather that Kahu took from the hair of his head was stuck in the ground to become a taniwha, or spirit monster, for that place.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah ini, sehelai bulu burung beo yang dicabut Kahu dari rambutnya ditancapkan di tanah agar menjadi taniwha, atau monster roh, bagi tempat itu.
claims.quote: so named by Kahu from a parrot-feather hou-kaka, which he took from the hair of his head, and stuck in the ground to become a taniwha or spirit monster for that place.

claims.statement: Kahu's companions embarked in a canoe, while he prevailed on a taniwha, or sea monster, of that place, named Paikea, to carry him on his back.
claims.statement_id: Rekan-rekan Kahu naik kano, sedangkan ia membujuk seekor taniwha, atau monster laut, di tempat itu bernama Paikea, untuk membawanya di punggungnya.
claims.quote: Here Kahu's companions embarked in a canoe, while he prevailed on a taniwha or sea monster of that place, named Paikea, to carry him on his back.

claims.statement: In the story narrated here the Taniwha (water-monster) lives in the caves of the rapid and has swallowed many a brave whose song was not powerful enough or displeased it; it broke the canoes on the large stones and took strong men and beautiful women into its dark cave for food.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah yang dituturkan di sini, sang Taniwha (monster air) tinggal di gua-gua jeram dan telah menelan banyak pemberani bila nyanyian mereka kurang kuat atau tidak menyenangkannya; ia memecahkan kano pada batu-batu besar dan membawa pria perkasa dan wanita cantik ke guanya yang gelap untuk dimakan.
claims.quote: as he narrates the story of the Taniwha, who lives in the caves of the rapid, and who has swallowed many a brave, when his song was not powerful enough or was displeasing to the Taniwha (water-monster). Then she broke the canoes on the large stones and took the strong men and beautiful women into her dark cave for food.

claims.statement: The book's glossary defines taniwha as a sea monster and water spirit.
claims.statement_id: Daftar istilah buku ini mendefinisikan taniwha sebagai monster laut dan roh air.
claims.quote: Taniwha: sea monster, water spirit.

claims.statement: Abaia is a huge, magical eel in Melanesian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Abaia adalah belut sakti berukuran raksasa dalam mitologi Melanesia.
claims.quote: Abaia is a huge, magical eel in Melanesian mythology.

claims.statement: The Abaia lives at the bottom of freshwater lakes in Fiji, the Solomon Islands, and Vanuatu.
claims.statement_id: Abaia mendiami dasar danau air tawar di kepulauan Fiji, Solomon, dan Vanuatu.
claims.quote: According to Melanesian mythology the Abaia is a type of large eel which dwells at the bottom of freshwater lakes in the Fiji, Solomon and Vanuatu Islands.

claims.statement: The creature considers all lake beings its children, defending them against harm or disturbance.
claims.statement_id: Abaia menganggap segenap satwa di danau sebagai anaknya dan membela mereka dari gangguan.
claims.quote: The beast is said to consider all creatures in the lake its children and protects them furiously against anyone who would harm or disturb them.

claims.statement: It is said that those foolish enough to catch fish from a lake containing the Abaia are immediately overwhelmed by a large wave caused by the thrashing of its powerful tail.
claims.statement_id: Konon, orang yang nekat menangkap ikan dari danau yang dihuni Abaia akan segera dihantam gelombang besar akibat hentakan ekor Abaia yang kuat.
claims.quote: It is said that those who are foolish enough to try to catch the fish from a lake containing the Abaia are immediately overwhelmed by a large wave caused by the thrashing of the Abaia's powerful tail.

claims.statement: According to another version, if someone harmed a creature living in the Abaia's home, the Abaia would cause a great rain storm flooding the land and drowning those who had caused the harm.
claims.statement_id: Menurut versi lain, jika seseorang mencelakai makhluk yang hidup di tempat tinggal Abaia, Abaia akan mendatangkan badai hujan besar yang membanjiri daratan dan menenggelamkan orang yang berbuat itu.
claims.quote: Another version of the legend states that if someone were to harm a creature living in the Abaia's home, the Abaia would cause a great rain storm flooding the land and drowning those who had caused the harm.

claims.statement: In one tale a man discovered a lake with many fish; at the bottom of the lake lived a magic eel, but the man did not know it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebuah kisah, seorang lelaki menemukan danau berisi banyak ikan; di dasar danau itu hidup belut sakti, tetapi lelaki itu tidak mengetahuinya.
claims.quote: One day a man discovered a lake in which were many fish; and at the bottom of the lake lived a magic eel, but the man knew it not.

claims.statement: In that tale one woman even laid hold of the great eel Abaia, who dwelt in the depths of the lake, though he escaped her.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah itu, seorang perempuan bahkan sempat memegang belut besar Abaia yang tinggal di kedalaman danau, meskipun Abaia lolos darinya.
claims.quote: while one woman even laid hold of the great eel, Abaia, who dwelt in the depths of the lake, though he escaped her.

claims.statement: Abaia was angry that his fish had been caught and that he himself had been seized, so that night he caused a great rain to fall and the lake waters rose; all the people drowned except an old woman who had not eaten of the fish and who saved herself in a tree.
claims.statement_id: Abaia marah karena ikannya ditangkap dan dirinya sendiri dicengkeram, sehingga malam itu ia mendatangkan hujan lebat dan air danau pun naik; semua orang tenggelam kecuali seorang perempuan tua yang tidak memakan ikan itu dan menyelamatkan diri di pohon.
claims.quote: Now Abaia was angry that his fish had been caught and that he himself had been seized, so he caused a great rain to fall that night, and the waters of the lake also rose, and all the people were drowned except an old woman who had not eaten of the fish and who saved herself in a tree.

claims.statement: According to the author, the association of snakes and eels with the deluge in these tales strongly suggests the type of deluge myth current in parts of Indonesia and apparently known also in the Cook Group.
claims.statement_id: Menurut pengarangnya, kaitan ular dan belut dengan air bah dalam kisah-kisah ini sangat mengisyaratkan jenis mitos air bah yang beredar di sebagian Indonesia dan tampaknya dikenal pula di Kepulauan Cook.
claims.quote: The association of snakes and eels with the deluge in these tales strongly suggests the type of deluge-myth current in parts of Indonesia, and known also apparently in the Cook Group.

claims.statement: Aku-Aku are humanoid spirits in the Rapa Nui mythology of Easter Island.
claims.statement_id: Aku-Aku adalah roh berwujud manusia dalam mitologi masyarakat Rapa Nui di Pulau Paskah.
claims.quote: Aku-Aku ('Devil', 'Ghost' or 'Spirit'), also known as Aku, Akuaku or Varua, are humanoid spirits in Rapa Nui mythology of the Easter Island.

claims.statement: Aku-Aku are spirits of the deceased that lack immortality and can be disposed of.
claims.statement_id: Aku-Aku adalah arwah orang mati yang tidak abadi serta bisa disingkirkan.
claims.quote: Aku-Aku are spirits of the dead, but they are not immortal and can be disposed of.

claims.statement: Ceremonial rituals are observed when entering caves considered to be Aku-Aku homes to avoid misfortune.
claims.statement_id: Ritual seremonial dilakukan ketika memasuki gua yang diyakini sebagai sarang Aku-Aku demi mencegah nasib buruk.
claims.quote: When entering caves, which were thought to be their homes, ceremonial rituals such as umu tahu can be performed to ward off bad luck or misfortune.

claims.statement: Aku-Aku can be of either sex, and different Aku-Aku are associated with particular areas of Easter Island.
claims.statement_id: Aku-Aku dapat berjenis kelamin laki-laki maupun perempuan, dan Aku-Aku yang berbeda dikaitkan dengan wilayah tertentu di Pulau Paskah.
claims.quote: They can be of either sex, and different Aku-Aku are associated with particular areas of the Easter Island.

claims.statement: The original group of Aku-Aku who arrived with Hotu Matuꞌa numbered around 90 and were generally cannibalistic in nature.
claims.statement_id: Kelompok Aku-Aku asli yang datang bersama Hotu Matuꞌa berjumlah sekitar 90 dan pada umumnya bersifat kanibal.
claims.quote: The original group of Aku-Aku who arrived with Hotu Matuꞌa numbered around 90, and were generally cannibalistic in nature.

claims.statement: There were stories of iva-atuas being employed to dispose of particularly violent Aku-Aku.
claims.statement_id: Ada cerita tentang iva-atua yang dipekerjakan untuk menyingkirkan Aku-Aku yang sangat ganas.
claims.quote: There were stories of iva-atuas being employed to dispose of particularly violent Aku-Aku.

claims.statement: Aku-Aku were not particularly worshiped, but were acknowledged before a meal. They were said to live off the aroma of a meal, and a "well-fed" and friendly Aku-Aku would take part in household chores for a family.
claims.statement_id: Aku-Aku tidak terlalu disembah, tetapi disapa sebelum santap. Konon mereka hidup dari aroma hidangan, dan Aku-Aku yang "kenyang" dan ramah akan ikut mengerjakan tugas rumah tangga sebuah keluarga.
claims.quote: Aku-Aku were not particularly worshiped, but they were acknowledged before a meal was taken. It was said that Aku-Aku live off the aroma of a meal. A 'well-fed' and friendly Aku-Aku would participate in household chores for a family.

claims.statement: The islanders term their old deities "aku-aku", which means spirits, or more frequently "tatane".
claims.statement_id: Penduduk pulau itu menyebut dewa-dewa lama mereka "aku-aku", yang berarti roh, atau lebih sering "tatane".
claims.quote: They term them “aku-aku,” which means spirits, or more frequently “tatane,”

claims.statement: Some of them were certainly spirits of the dead that had probably become deified; the ancestors of Hotu-matua were reported to have come with him to the island.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian dari mereka pasti roh orang mati yang mungkin telah didewakan; leluhur Hotu-matua dilaporkan ikut datang bersamanya ke pulau.
claims.quote: some of them were certainly the spirits of the dead, but had probably become deified; the ancestors of Hotu-matua were reported to have come with him to the island.

claims.statement: They existed in large numbers, both male and female, each connected with a different part of the island; a list of about ninety was given, with their places of residence.
claims.statement_id: Jumlah mereka banyak, laki-laki dan perempuan, dan masing-masing berkaitan dengan bagian pulau yang berbeda; disebutkan daftar sekitar sembilan puluh nama beserta tempat tinggalnya.
claims.quote: They existed in large numbers, being both male and female, and were connected with different parts of the island; a list of about ninety was given, with their places of residence.

claims.statement: The aku-aku were amiable or the reverse according to whether or not they were well fed; if hungry, they ate women and children.
claims.statement_id: Aku-Aku ramah atau sebaliknya tergantung apakah mereka cukup diberi makan; bila lapar, mereka memangsa perempuan dan anak-anak.
claims.quote: the aku-aku, in this at least being human, were amiable or the reverse according to whether or not they were well fed. If they were hungry, they ate women and children,

claims.statement: If well-disposed to a man, the aku-aku would do work for him, so that he would wake in the morning to find his potato field dug.
claims.statement_id: Bila berkenan pada seseorang, Aku-Aku mau bekerja untuknya, sehingga pagi harinya ia mendapati ladang kentangnya sudah tergali.
claims.quote: if, on the contrary, they were well-disposed to a man, they would do work for him, and he would wake in the morning to find his potato-field dug,

claims.statement: The aku-aku appeared in human form, in which they were indistinguishable from ordinary persons.
claims.statement_id: Aku-Aku tampil dalam wujud manusia dan tidak bisa dibedakan dari orang biasa.
claims.quote: The aku-aku appeared in human form, in which they were indistinguishable from ordinary persons.

claims.statement: An aku-aku known as Uka-o-hoheru looked like a very beautiful woman and was the wife of a young Tupahotu who had no idea she was really a tatane.
claims.statement_id: Seorang aku-aku bernama Uka-o-hoheru tampak seperti perempuan yang sangat cantik dan menjadi istri seorang pemuda Tupahotu yang tidak tahu bahwa ia sebenarnya tatane.
claims.quote: One known as Uka-o-hoheru looked like a very beautiful woman, and was the wife of a young Tupahotu who had no idea she was really a tatane.

claims.statement: Aku-aku were not immortal. A man called Raraku, said to have given his name to the mountain, caught a big "heke", which seems to have been an octopus, in the sea near Tongariki and ate it, with the result that he went mad and all people gave chase to him.
claims.statement_id: Aku-aku tidak abadi. Seorang lelaki bernama Raraku, yang konon menjadi asal nama gunung itu, menangkap seekor "heke" besar yang tampaknya gurita di laut dekat Tongariki lalu memakannya hingga ia gila, dan semua orang mengejarnya.
claims.quote: Aku-aku were not immortal. A man called Raraku, after whom the mountain is said to have been named, caught a big “heke,” which seems to have been an octopus, in the sea near Tongariki and ate it, with the result that he went mad, and all people gave chase to him.

claims.statement: He seized a wooden lizard and, using it as a club, ran amok among the tatane across the north shore and down the west coast, killing them right and left; the names of twenty-three who met their fate this way were given.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kegilaannya ia mengambil kadal kayu dan memakainya sebagai pentungan, mengamuk di antara para tatane di pantai utara hingga pantai barat dan membunuh mereka; disebutkan nama dua puluh tiga yang tewas dengan cara itu.
claims.quote: He caught up a wooden lizard (fig. 117), and, using it as a club, ran amok among tatane across the north shore and down the west coast, killing them right and left; the names of twenty-three were given who thus met their fate.

claims.statement: Human beings, in turn, were liable to be attacked by tatane, especially at night, when not only their bodies but also their own spirits were at risk.
claims.statement_id: Manusia, sebaliknya, bisa diserang tatane, terutama pada malam hari, ketika bukan hanya tubuh mereka yang terancam tetapi juga roh mereka sendiri.
claims.quote: Human beings, on the other hand, were liable to be attacked by tatane, more particularly at night, when there was risk, not only to their bodies, but also to their own spirits

claims.statement: The aku-aku Mata-wara-wara ("Strong-Rain") had a partner, the aku-aku Papai-a-taki-vera: Mata was to bring on rain while Papai built a house of reeds that existed only at night.
claims.statement_id: Aku-aku Mata-wara-wara ("Hujan-Deras") bermitra dengan aku-aku Papai-a-taki-vera: Mata mendatangkan hujan, sementara Papai membangun rumah alang-alang yang hanya ada pada malam hari.
claims.quote: the aku-aku Mata-wara-wara, or “Strong-Rain.” He had as a partner another aku-aku called Papai-a-taki-vera, and they arranged between them that Mata should bring on rain, while Papai constructed a house of reeds which was only there at night

claims.statement: When the spirits of sleeping people, wandering abroad, became cold with the rain, they went into the house and the tatane killed them.
claims.statement_id: Ketika roh orang yang sedang tidur, yang berkelana ke luar, kedinginan oleh hujan, roh-roh itu masuk ke rumah itu dan para tatane membunuh mereka.
claims.quote: then when the spirits of sleeping people, which were wandering abroad, became cold with the rain, they went into the house and the tatane killed them.

claims.statement: There was a class known as "ivi-atua", including both men and women; the most important of them, perhaps ten in the island, held commune with the aku-aku.
claims.statement_id: Ada golongan yang disebut "ivi-atua", mencakup laki-laki dan perempuan; yang terpenting di antara mereka, mungkin sepuluh orang di pulau itu, berhubungan dengan aku-aku.
claims.quote: the class known as “ivi-atua,” which included both men and women. The most important of these ivi-atua, of whom it was said there might be perhaps ten in the island, held commune with the aku-aku,

claims.statement: On the whole the female wooden figures and those with ribs seem to have been considered supernatural beings, generally called aku-aku and sometimes atua, while the others represent men.
claims.statement_id: Pada umumnya patung kayu perempuan dan yang berusuk dianggap makhluk gaib; patung-patung itu biasanya disebut aku-aku, kadang atua, sedangkan yang lain menggambarkan manusia.
claims.quote: on the whole the female figures and those with ribs seem to have been considered to be supernatural beings; they are generally called aku-aku, and sometimes atua, while the others represent men.

claims.statement: Wooden kavakava figurines represent Aku-Aku.
claims.statement_id: Figurin kayu kavakava dipakai untuk melambangkan Aku-Aku.
claims.quote: Wooden kavakava (carved figurines) representing Aku-Aku

claims.statement: Apukohai is a marine monster in the mythology of Kauaʻi.
claims.statement_id: Apukohai adalah monster laut dalam mitologi pulau Kauaʻi.
claims.quote: Apukohai is a marine monster in the mythology of the island of Kauaʻi.

claims.statement: The giant hero Kawelo met Apukohai while voyaging to Oʻahu.
claims.statement_id: Raksasa sakti Kawelo bertemu dengan Apukohai saat berlayar ke Oʻahu.
claims.quote: Kawelo, a giant of enormous strength, departs for Oʻahu and encounters Apukohai.

claims.statement: Following a fierce struggle, Kawelo killed Apukohai with help from the owl god and the fish Ulu-makaikai.
claims.statement_id: Setelah perkelahian hebat, Kawelo menewaskan Apukohai berkat bantuan dewa burung hantu dan ikan Ulu-makaikai.
claims.quote: After a fierce struggle, Kawelo kills Apukohai, having invoked the assistance of the owl god and the fish Ulu-makaikai (Beckwith 1970: 409–411).

claims.statement: In the Remy-Brigham version, Kawelo is a giant of prodigious strength.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Remy-Brigham, Kawelo adalah raksasa dengan kekuatan luar biasa.
claims.quote: Remy-Brigham version. Kawelo is a giant of prodigious strength.

claims.statement: Kawelo, a giant of prodigious strength, is welcomed by Kakuhihewa and secretly collects an expedition; he sets out for an island and meets "evil monsters in the shape of the marine monster Apukohai", invoking the owl god and the fish Uhu-makaikai, which he traps in a net.
claims.statement_id: Kawelo, raksasa berkekuatan luar biasa, disambut Kakuhihewa dan diam-diam menghimpun pasukan; ia berangkat ke sebuah pulau dan bertemu "monster jahat" berwujud monster laut Apukohai, dengan menyeru dewa burung hantu dan ikan Uhu-makaikai yang ia jerat dalam jaring.
claims.quote: Remy-Brigham version. Kawelo is a giant of prodigious strength. ... He is welcomed by Kakuhihewa and secretly collects an expedition against Kauai. He sets out for that island and en-counters evil monsters in the shape of the marine monster Apukohai, against whom he invokes the owl god, and the fish Uhu-makaikai, which he traps in a net

claims.statement: In the comic series Sherman's Lagoon, Apukohai is shown as a figure in a huge Tiki mask who fires lightning bolts from the clouds.
claims.statement_id: Dalam serial komik Sherman's Lagoon, Apukohai digambarkan sebagai sosok bertopeng tiki raksasa yang melepaskan sambaran petir dari awan.
claims.quote: Sherman's Lagoon - In a series of comics, Apukohai is represented as a guy with a huge Tiki mask who fires lightning bolts (and his kitchen sink) from the clouds.

claims.statement: Dakuwaqa is a shark deity in Fijian mythology who guards the islands as a fierce sea monster.
claims.statement_id: Dakuwaqa adalah dewa hiu penjaga kepulauan Fiji yang kerap menjelma sebagai monster laut ganas.
claims.quote: In Fijian mythology, Dakuwaqa (Dakuwanga) is a shark deity and often appears as a fierce sea monster, guarding the islands.

claims.statement: Fishermen respected Dakuwaqa because he protected them from sea dangers and predators.
claims.statement_id: Dakuwaqa dihormati para nelayan karena melindungi mereka dari mara bahaya di laut.
claims.quote: He was greatly respected by fishermen because he protected them from any danger at sea and its denizens.

claims.statement: Dakuwaqa can shapeshift, but his true form combines a muscular man with a shark upper body.
claims.statement_id: Dakuwaqa dapat beralih rupa, namun wujud sejatinya adalah pria kekar dengan tubuh bagian atas berupa hiu.
claims.quote: Dakuwaqa can also change shape into anything, but his real form is that of a muscular Fijian man with the upper torso of a shark.

claims.statement: In one creation myth the god was planning to conquer Kadavu Island by way of the river when the goddess Rokobakaniceva challenged him in the form of an octopus.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu mitos penciptaan, sang dewa berencana menaklukkan Pulau Kadavu lewat sungai ketika dewi Rokobakaniceva menantangnya dalam wujud gurita.
claims.quote: In one creation myth, the god was planning inland to conquer Kadavu Island through the river when the goddess Rokobakaniceva challenged him in the form of an octopus.

claims.statement: After a great battle the octopus won by pulling out his teeth with her eight arms, holding off Dakuwaqa's massive attack and forcing him to promise never to attack Kadavu again.
claims.statement_id: Setelah pertempuran besar, gurita itu menang dengan mencabut gigi Dakuwaqa memakai kedelapan lengannya, menahan serangan dahsyatnya, dan memaksa Dakuwaqa berjanji tidak akan menyerang Kadavu lagi.
claims.quote: After a great battle, the octopus won by pulling out his teeth with her eight arms which enabled her to hold off the massive attack of Dakuwaqa, forcing Dakuwaqa to promise to never attack Kadavu again.

claims.statement: That is how Dakuwaqa became the god and protector of Kadavu.
claims.statement_id: Demikianlah Dakuwaqa menjadi dewa dan pelindung Kadavu.
claims.quote: That is how Dakuwaqa became the god and protector of Kadavu.

claims.statement: In an account quoted there, a witness described a great fish of near 60 feet, brown-spotted, with the head of a shark and the tail of a whale, that rose under his ship and almost capsized it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam catatan yang dikutip, seorang saksi menggambarkan ikan besar sepanjang sekitar 60 kaki, berbintik cokelat, berkepala hiu dan berekor paus, yang muncul di bawah kapalnya dan nyaris membaliknya.
claims.quote: A great fish, which he described as near 60 feet in length, brown-spotted and mottled on its back, with the head of a shark and the tail of a whale, came up under his ship, almost capsizing it.

claims.statement: The crew followed the ancient pattern, pouring a strong libation of kava into the sea, which seemed just the right idea for placating fish-gods; the monster slowly submerged, and to the Fijian crew this was "Dakuwaqa", in the twentieth century.
claims.statement_id: Awak kapal menuruti pola kuno dengan menuangkan kava ke laut sebagai persembahan yang tampaknya tepat untuk menenangkan dewa ikan; monster itu perlahan tenggelam, dan bagi awak Fiji itu adalah "Dakuwaqa" pada abad kedua puluh.
claims.quote: followed the ancient pattern, pouring a strong libation of kava into the sea, which, it would seem, was just the right idea for placating fish-gods; the monster slowly submerged ... To the Fijian crew this was the "Dakuwaqa"--in the twentieth century

claims.statement: In the DC Universe, Dakuwaqa is the father of the supervillain King Shark.
claims.statement_id: Dalam semesta DC, Dakuwaqa adalah ayah dari penjahat super King Shark.
claims.quote: Dakuwaqa is the father of the supervillain King Shark in the DC Universe.

claims.statement: Jeff VanderMeer wrote the story The Third Bear about Dakuwaqa.
claims.statement_id: Jeff VanderMeer menulis cerita The Third Bear tentang Dakuwaqa.
claims.quote: Jeff VanderMeer wrote the story The Third Bear about Dakuwaqa.

claims.statement: In Fiji there are two ancestral shark gods; the names of both are linked to boats, particularly to the sail, which is shaped like a shark fin.
claims.statement_id: Di Fiji ada dua dewa hiu leluhur; nama keduanya berkaitan dengan perahu, terutama layar yang berbentuk seperti sirip hiu.
claims.quote: In Fiji, there are two ancestral shark gods. The names of both are linked to boats, particularly to the sail, which is shaped like a shark fin.

claims.statement: Dakuwaqa means "back of the boat", with daku the back and waqa the boat.
claims.statement_id: Dakuwaqa berarti "bagian belakang perahu", dengan daku berarti bagian belakang dan waqa berarti perahu.
claims.quote: Dakuwaqa (Ndah-koo-wah-ngah) means ‘back of the boat’, with daku the back and waqa the boat.

claims.statement: Masilaca, the other ancestral shark god named on that page, comes from masi (bark cloth, also a shark's fin) and laca (sail).
claims.statement_id: Masilaca, dewa hiu leluhur Fiji yang lain di halaman itu, berasal dari masi (kain kulit kayu, juga sirip hiu) dan laca (layar).
claims.quote: Masilaca (Masi-lah-thah) comes from masi, which is bark cloth (and also a shark’s fin) and laca, which is sail.

claims.statement: A villager says that people of his village chose the sharks as their god, a sea god worshipped whenever they need something; his name is Dakuwaqa, very powerful and still powerful today.
claims.statement_id: Seorang warga desa menuturkan bahwa kampungnya memilih hiu sebagai dewa, dewa laut yang disembah saat mereka butuh sesuatu; namanya Dakuwaqa, sangat kuat dan masih kuat hingga kini.
claims.quote: the people from my village, they choose the sharks to be their god. So it's a sea god. Every time they need something, they just worship the sea god. So his name is Dakuwaqa. Is very powerful and is still powerful today.

claims.statement: According to the villager, every time Dakuwaqa comes to the village he changes himself into a human being.
claims.statement_id: Menurut warga desa itu, setiap kali Dakuwaqa datang ke desa ia mengubah dirinya menjadi manusia.
claims.quote: Every time he comes to the village, he change himself to be a human being.

claims.statement: Ratu Sir Penaia Ganilau, one of Fiji's highest chiefs and the nation's first president after independence, is a descendant of the ancestral shark god Dakuwaqa.
claims.statement_id: Ratu Sir Penaia Ganilau, salah satu kepala adat tertinggi Fiji dan presiden pertama setelah kemerdekaan Fiji, adalah keturunan dewa hiu leluhur Dakuwaqa.
claims.quote: The late Ratu Sir Penaia Ganilau, one of Fiji's highest chiefs and the nation's first president, following Fiji's Independence in 1987, is a descendant of the ancestral shark god Dakuwaqa.

claims.statement: Mourners reported a school of sharks surfacing and accompanying the vessel out to sea; sharks are rarely seen in Suva Harbor, but it came as no surprise because of Ganilau's connection to Dakuwaqa.
claims.statement_id: Para pelayat melaporkan sekawanan hiu muncul dan mengiringi kapal ke laut; hiu jarang terlihat di Pelabuhan Suva, tetapi hal itu tidak mengejutkan karena kaitan Ganilau dengan Dakuwaqa.
claims.quote: Mourners reported a school of sharks surfacing and accompanying the vessel out to sea. Shark sighting in Suva Harbor is rare, but on this occasion, it did not come as a surprise because of Ganilau’s connection to Dakuwaqa.

claims.statement: A villager states that the shark is part of their culture going back to before Christianity, many hundreds of years ago.
claims.statement_id: Seorang warga desa menyatakan bahwa hiu adalah bagian budaya mereka sejak sebelum agama Kristen, ratusan tahun lampau.
claims.quote: Shark is part of our culture going back to before Christianity, going back many, many hundreds and hundreds of years ago.

claims.statement: The legend of Fisher's ghost is a popular Australian folk tale dating to the early 19th century.
claims.statement_id: Legenda hantu Fisher adalah kisah hantu Australia populer yang berakar sejak awal abad ke-19.
claims.quote: The legend of Fisher's ghost is a popular Australian ghost story or folk tale dating to the early 19th century.

claims.statement: The story arose from historical occurrences in Campbelltown, New South Wales.
claims.statement_id: Kisah ini lahir dari peristiwa nyata di Campbelltown, New South Wales.
claims.quote: It arose from a series of historical events which occurred in Campbelltown, New South Wales, now a large urban population centre on the southwestern outskirts of Sydney, but at the time a remote rural outpost.

claims.statement: The Festival of Fisher's Ghost has been held in Campbelltown since 1956 inspired by the lore.
claims.statement_id: Festival of Fisher's Ghost dirayakan di Campbelltown sejak 1956 terilhami oleh legenda tersebut.
claims.quote: Inspired by the legend, the Festival of Fisher's Ghost has been celebrated in Campbelltown since 1956.

claims.statement: On 17 June 1826 Frederick Fisher, an English-born farmer from Campbelltown, suddenly disappeared.
claims.statement_id: Pada 17 Juni 1826, petani kelahiran Inggris dari Campbelltown bernama Frederick Fisher tiba-tiba menghilang.
claims.quote: On 17 June 1826 an English-born Australian farmer from Campbelltown named Frederick Fisher (born 28 August 1792 in London) suddenly disappeared.

claims.statement: His friend and neighbour George Worrall claimed Fisher had returned to England and had given him power of attorney over his property and affairs before leaving.
claims.statement_id: Teman sekaligus tetangganya, George Worrall, mengaku Fisher telah pulang ke Inggris dan sebelum pergi memberinya kuasa atas harta dan urusannya.
claims.quote: His friend and neighbour George Worrall claimed that Fisher had returned to his native England, and that before departing had given him power of attorney over his property and general affairs.

claims.statement: Four months after Fisher's disappearance a respectable local man, John Farley, ran into the local hotel agitated and told the patrons he had seen the ghost of Fred Fisher sitting on the rail of a nearby bridge.
claims.statement_id: Empat bulan setelah Fisher menghilang, seorang warga terpandang bernama John Farley berlari ke hotel setempat dengan gelisah dan mengatakan telah melihat hantu Fred Fisher duduk di pagar jembatan terdekat.
claims.quote: Four months after Fisher's disappearance a respectable local man named John Farley, ran into the local hotel in a very agitated state. He told the astonished patrons that he had seen the ghost of Fred Fisher sitting on the rail of a nearby bridge.

claims.statement: Farley related that the ghost had not spoken but had merely pointed to a paddock beyond the creek before disappearing.
claims.statement_id: Farley bercerita bahwa hantu itu tidak berbicara, hanya menunjuk ke sebuah padang di seberang kali, lalu menghilang.
claims.quote: Farley related that the ghost had not spoken, but had merely pointed to a paddock beyond the creek, before disappearing.

claims.statement: The circumstances of Fisher's disappearance eventually aroused enough suspicion that police searched the paddock the ghost had pointed to, and the remains of the murdered Fisher were found buried by the side of a creek.
claims.statement_id: Keadaan di sekitar hilangnya Fisher akhirnya menimbulkan kecurigaan yang cukup sehingga polisi menggeledah padang yang ditunjuk hantu itu, dan jasad Fisher yang dibunuh ditemukan terkubur di tepi sebuah kali.
claims.quote: the circumstances surrounding Fisher's disappearance eventually aroused sufficient suspicion that a police search of the paddock to which the ghost had pointed was undertaken - during which the remains of the murdered Fisher were discovered buried by the side of a creek.

claims.statement: George Worrall was arrested for the crime, confessed, and was subsequently hanged.
claims.statement_id: George Worrall ditangkap atas kejahatan itu, mengaku, lalu digantung.
claims.quote: George Worrall was arrested for the crime, confessed, and subsequently hanged.

claims.statement: It has been suggested that Farley invented the ghost story to conceal some other source of his knowledge of where Fisher's body lay, but this cannot be confirmed.
claims.statement_id: Pernah diusulkan bahwa Farley mengarang kisah hantu itu untuk menutupi sumber pengetahuan lain tentang letak jasad Fisher, tetapi hal ini tidak dapat dipastikan.
claims.quote: It has been suggested that Farley invented the ghost story as a way of concealing some other speculated source of his knowledge about the whereabouts of Fisher's body, but this cannot be confirmed.

claims.statement: Joe Nickell has written that the ghost story may have originated from an anonymous 1832 poem that fictionalised Fisher and Worrall.
claims.statement_id: Joe Nickell menulis bahwa kisah hantu itu mungkin berasal dari sebuah puisi anonim tahun 1832 yang memfiksikan Fisher dan Worrall.
claims.quote: Joe Nickell has written the ghost story may have originated from an anonymous poem in 1832 which fictionalised Fisher and Worrall.

claims.statement: Contemporary police and court records do not mention the ghost story.
claims.statement_id: Catatan polisi dan pengadilan sezaman tidak menyebut kisah hantu itu.
claims.quote: Contemporary police and court records do not mention the ghost story.

claims.statement: The legend of Fisher's ghost later entered popular folklore, and the creek beside which the body was found is known as Fisher's Ghost Creek.
claims.statement_id: Legenda hantu Fisher kemudian masuk ke cerita rakyat populer, dan kali tempat jasad itu ditemukan dikenal sebagai Fisher's Ghost Creek.
claims.quote: The legend of Fisher's ghost has since entered popular folklore and the creek beside which the body was discovered is known as Fisher's Ghost Creek,

claims.statement: A 1924 Australian silent film titled Fisher's Ghost retells the events of the legend.
claims.statement_id: Film bisu Australia tahun 1924 berjudul Fisher's Ghost menceritakan ulang peristiwa dalam legenda itu.
claims.quote: A 1924 Australian silent film titled Fisher's Ghost retells the events of the legend.

claims.statement: Fishers Ghost Creek runs through Campbelltown's Koshiga and Bradbury parks and commemorates the 1826 murder of the convict Frederick Fisher.
claims.statement_id: Fishers Ghost Creek mengalir melalui Koshiga Park dan Bradbury Park di Campbelltown dan memperingati pembunuhan narapidana Frederick Fisher pada 1826.
claims.quote: Fishers Ghost Creek runs through Campbelltown's Koshiga and Bradbury parks, and commemorates the murder of the convict Frederick Fisher in 1826.

claims.statement: Worrall claimed his neighbour had gone "home", but this was unconvincing because Fisher was still a convict and risked arrest if he reappeared in England.
claims.statement_id: Worrall mengaku tetangganya pergi "pulang", tetapi hal itu tidak meyakinkan karena Fisher masih narapidana dan berisiko ditangkap bila muncul lagi di Inggris.
claims.quote: Worrall claimed that his neighbour had gone 'home', but this was unconvincing, because Fisher was still a convict and risked arrest if he reappeared in England.

claims.statement: On 25 October 1826 two boys reported seeing bloodstains on a fence at Fisher's farm.
claims.statement_id: Pada 25 Oktober 1826 dua anak laki-laki melaporkan melihat noda darah pada pagar di pertanian Fisher.
claims.quote: On 25 October 1826 two boys reported seeing bloodstains on a fence at Fisher's farm.

claims.statement: After new searches uncovered a lock of hair and a tooth, the police called in Gilbert, an Aboriginal tracker from Liverpool, who tasted water in the marshy land and then led them to Fisher's grave on Worrall's land; Worrall was tried and hanged in February 1827.
claims.statement_id: Setelah pencarian baru menemukan sehelai rambut dan sebuah gigi, polisi memanggil Gilbert, pelacak Aborigin dari Liverpool, yang mencicipi air di tanah rawa lalu menuntun polisi ke makam Fisher di tanah Worrall; Worrall diadili dan digantung pada Februari 1827.
claims.quote: When new searches uncovered a lock of hair and a tooth, the police called in Gilbert, an Aboriginal tracker from Liverpool. He tasted water in the marshy land and proclaimed 'white fellow's fat there', before leading the police to Fisher's grave on Worrall's land. Worrall was tried and hanged in February 1827.

claims.statement: Rumours circulated in Campbelltown that the finding of his body was no accident, and the story of Fisher's ghost has been retold in print since the early 1830s.
claims.statement_id: Desas-desus beredar di Campbelltown bahwa penemuan jasadnya bukan kebetulan, dan kisah hantu Fisher telah dicetak ulang sejak awal 1830-an.
claims.quote: Rumours circulated in Campbelltown that the finding of his body was not accidental – and the story of Fisher's ghost has been retold in print since the early 1830s.

claims.statement: The best-known version says the body stayed undiscovered until a farmer named Farley, returning home from Patrick's Inn, met Fisher's ghost sitting on the rail at the bridge over Queen Street; the spectre beckoned and pointed back towards Worrall's land.
claims.statement_id: Versi terkenal menyebut jasad itu tak ditemukan sampai seorang petani bernama Farley, yang pulang dari Patrick's Inn, bertemu hantu Fisher duduk di pagar jembatan di atas Queen Street; sosok itu melambai dan menunjuk kembali ke tanah Worrall.
claims.quote: The best-known version states that the body remained undiscovered until a local farmer named Farley was returning home from Patrick's Inn and encountered Fisher's ghost sitting on the rail at the bridge over Queen Street. The spectre beckoned to him and pointed back towards Worrall's land.

claims.statement: "Fisher's Ghost" has become an essential element of Campbelltown's collective memory; the story is re-enacted in a festival held there every year since 1960.
claims.statement_id: "Fisher's Ghost" telah menjadi unsur penting ingatan kolektif Campbelltown; kisahnya dipentaskan ulang dalam festival yang digelar di sana setiap tahun sejak 1960.
claims.quote: 'Fisher's Ghost' has become an essential element of Campbelltown's collective memory: the story is re-enacted as part of a festival held there every year since 1960.

claims.statement: The mythical spirit was supposed to have appeared sitting on a fence pointing to where Fisher's body lay buried; the story first appeared in print in the poem "The Sprite of the Creek" in the weekly sporting journal "Hill's Life in New South Wales" in August 1832.
claims.statement_id: Roh mitos itu konon tampak duduk di pagar sambil menunjuk tempat jasad Fisher terkubur; kisahnya pertama kali tercetak dalam puisi "The Sprite of the Creek" di majalah olahraga mingguan "Hill's Life in New South Wales" pada Agustus 1832.
claims.quote: The mythical spirit was supposed to have appeared sitting on a fence pointing to where Fisher's body lay buried. The ghost story first appeared in print in the poem 'The Sprite of the Creek' published in the weekly sporting journal 'Hill's Life in New South Wales' in August 1832.
