claims.statement: The Rainbow Serpent is a common creator deity in Australian Aboriginal traditions.
claims.statement_id: Ular Pelangi adalah dewa umum yang kerap dipandang sebagai dewa pencipta dalam masyarakat Aborigin Australia.
claims.quote: The Rainbow Serpent or Rainbow Snake is a common deity, often seen as the creator god, known by numerous names in different Australian Aboriginal languages by the many different Aboriginal peoples.

claims.statement: Julunggul or Yurlunggur is the name of the rainbow serpent among the Murngin (Yolngu) in Arnhem Land.
claims.statement_id: Julunggul atau Yurlunggur adalah nama ular pelangi bagi kelompok Murngin (Yolngu) di Arnhem Land.
claims.quote: Yurlunggur is the name of the "rainbow serpent" according to the Murngin (a Yolngu group) in north-eastern Arnhem Land, also styled Yurlungur, Yulunggur, Jurlungur, Julunggur or Julunggul.

claims.statement: The Yurlunggur was regarded as the great father.
claims.statement_id: Yurlunggur dianggap sebagai sosok 'sang bapa agung'.
claims.quote: The Yurlunggur was considered "the great father".

claims.statement: While single-headed, the Yurlunggur of Arnhem Land may possess a double body.
claims.statement_id: Meskipun berkepala tunggal, Yurlunggur dari Arnhem Land mungkin berbadan ganda.
claims.quote: While it is single-headed, the Yurlunggur of Arnhem land may possess a double-body.

claims.statement: Yulunggul is the Great Python of north-central Arnhem Land, who swallowed the Wawalag sisters and their child(ren).
claims.statement_id: Yulunggul adalah Piton Agung dari Arnhem Land bagian utara-tengah, yang menelan saudari-saudari Wawalag beserta anak mereka.
claims.quote: Yulunggul is the Great Python of north-central Arnhem Land, who swallowed the Wawalag sisters and their child(ren).

claims.statement: Yulunggul is most often identified as male, with or without female counterparts; one northeastern Arnhem Land version has Yulunggul as female but with symbolic male (phallic) implications.
claims.statement_id: Yulunggul paling sering dikenali sebagai jantan, dengan atau tanpa pasangan betina; satu versi dari timur laut Arnhem Land menyebutnya betina tetapi bermakna simbolis jantan (falus).
claims.quote: Yulunggul is most often identified as male, with or without female counterparts. One northeastern Arnhem Land version specifies Yulunggul as female but with symbolic male (phallic) implications.

claims.statement: William Lloyd Warner's 1937 account notes a variety of snakes, goannas, and snails as sons of Yulunggul.
claims.statement_id: Catatan William Lloyd Warner (1937) menyebut berbagai ular, biawak, dan siput sebagai anak-anak Yulunggul.
claims.quote: William Lloyd Warner's account (1937, e.g. p. 257) notes a variety of snakes, goannas, and snails as sons of Yulunggul.

claims.statement: Warner calls Yulunggul "great father" (Yindi Bapa or Bapa Yindi), but he may have misheard the more usual expression "great snake" (Yindi Baapi).
claims.statement_id: Warner menyebut Yulunggul "bapa agung" (Yindi Bapa atau Bapa Yindi), tetapi mungkin ia salah dengar ungkapan yang lebih lazim, "ular agung" (Yindi Baapi).
claims.quote: Warner refers to Yulunggul as "great father" (Yindi Bapa or Bapa Yindi), but it is possible that he misheard the more usual expression, "great snake" (Yindi Baapi).

claims.statement: Unlike many great mythic characters who came from elsewhere, Yulunggul had always been at his special water hole, known as Mirara-minar and Muruwul.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dari banyak tokoh mitos besar yang datang dari tempat lain, Yulunggul selalu berada di lubang air khususnya, yang dikenal sebagai Mirara-minar dan Muruwul.
claims.quote: Unlike so many of the great mythic characters, who came from elsewhere to sites that were to be spiritually associated with them, Yulunggul had always been at his special water hole, known as Mirara-minar and Muruwul;

claims.statement: All the mythic Snakes in north and northeastern Arnhem Land, including Yulunggul, were good site guardians and knew who the travellers were.
claims.statement_id: Semua Ular mitos di Arnhem Land utara dan timur laut, termasuk Yulunggul, adalah penjaga situs yang baik dan tahu siapa para pengelana itu.
claims.quote: all of the mythic Snakes in north and northeastern Arnhem Land, including Yulunggul, were good site guardians and knew who the travelers were.

claims.statement: There are divergent views on whether Yulunggul is a Rainbow Snake manifestation.
claims.statement_id: Ada pandangan yang berbeda tentang apakah Yulunggul merupakan perwujudan Ular Pelangi.
claims.quote: There are divergent views on whether Yulunggul is a Rainbow Snake manifestation.

claims.statement: Where his Rainbow Snake identification is not accepted, mainly in eastern Arnhem Land, it is sometimes explained: "Yulunggul is separate: he is himself."
claims.statement_id: Di tempat identifikasinya sebagai Ular Pelangi tidak diterima, terutama di sisi timur Arnhem Land, kadang dijelaskan bahwa "Yulunggul terpisah: ia adalah dirinya sendiri".
claims.quote: Where his Rainbow Snake identification is not accepted, mainly on the eastern side of Arnhem Land, it is sometimes explained with, "Yulunggul is separate: he is himself."

claims.statement: He is the spirit of the monsoon, the west and northwest wind that brings the fertilizing rains of the wet season.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah roh musim hujan monsun, angin barat dan barat laut yang membawa hujan penyubur musim basah.
claims.quote: He is the spirit of the monsoon, the west and northwest wind that brings the fertilizing rains of the wet season.

claims.statement: In some Milingimbi versions he flies across the country with the Wawalag and their child(ren) inside him, naming various places and allocating local dialects.
claims.statement_id: Dalam beberapa versi Milingimbi, ia terbang melintasi negeri dengan Wawalag dan anak mereka di dalam tubuhnya, menamai berbagai tempat dan membagikan dialek setempat.
claims.quote: In some Milingimbi versions (Warner, p. 254), he flies across the country with the Wawalag and their child(ren) inside him, naming various places and allocating local dialects.

claims.statement: Just as the copulations of the Snakes and clouds in the wet season ensure fertility in the dry season, Yulunggul's "union" with the Wawalag made him a symbol of seasonal fertility.
claims.statement_id: Seperti persetubuhan para Ular dan awan pada musim basah menjamin kesuburan musim kering, "persatuan" Yulunggul dengan Wawalag menjadikannya lambang kesuburan musiman.
claims.quote: Just as the copulations of the Snakes and clouds during the wet season ensure fertility in the dry season, so Yulunggul's "union" with the Wawalag transformed him into a symbol of seasonal fertility.

claims.statement: The didjeridu that features so prominently in Kunapipi and associated rituals is Yulunggul, and its sound is his voice.
claims.statement_id: Didjeridu yang menonjol dalam Kunapipi dan ritual terkait adalah Yulunggul, dan bunyinya adalah suaranya.
claims.quote: The didjeridu that features so prominently in Kunapipi and associated rituals, however, is Yulunggul, and its sound is his voice.

claims.statement: In a Milingimbi version, a great Yulunggul didjeridu came out of his water hole and revived the sisters with the help of green ants; Yulunggul was angry, "killed" them and swallowed them again.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu versi Milingimbi, didjeridu Yulunggul keluar dari lubang airnya dan menghidupkan kembali para saudari dengan bantuan semut hijau; Yulunggul marah, "membunuh" mereka, dan menelannya lagi.
claims.quote: in a Milingimbi version that is found only in Warner, after Yulunggul had regurgitated the sisters and they lay "dead," a great Yulunggul didjeridu (drone pipe) came out of Yulunggul's water hole of its own volition and revived them with the help of green ants. Yulunggul was angry. He "killed" the sisters and swallowed them again.

claims.statement: Yulunggul has both freshwater and saltwater affiliations.
claims.statement_id: Yulunggul berkaitan dengan air tawar maupun air asin.
claims.quote: He has both freshwater and saltwater affiliations.

claims.statement: In one of his roles Yulunggul is explicitly a culture-area indicator or boundary marker; in his conversation with the other great Snakes after swallowing the Wawalag he faces east.
claims.statement_id: Dalam salah satu perannya Yulunggul secara eksplisit adalah penanda wilayah budaya atau batas; dalam percakapannya dengan Ular besar lain setelah menelan Wawalag, ia menghadap timur.
claims.quote: In one of his roles Yulunggul is, explicitly, a culture-area indicator, or a boundary marker. During his conversation with the other great Snakes after he has swallowed the Wawalag, he faces east.

claims.statement: Nightmarchers are deadly ghosts of ancient tribal Hawaiian warriors.
claims.statement_id: Nightmarchers adalah arwah mematikan prajurit kuno suku Hawaii.
claims.quote: In Hawaiian mythology, Nightmarchers (huakaʻi pō) or Spirit Ranks (ʻoiʻo) are the deadly ghosts of ancient tribal Hawaiian warriors.

claims.statement: The nightmarchers serve as the vanguard for a sacred ruler or noble.
claims.statement_id: Nightmarchers bertindak sebagai garda pengawal untuk raja atau kepala suku yang suci.
claims.quote: The nightmarchers are the vanguard for a sacred king, chief, or chiefess.

claims.statement: They march in group formation throughout the night from sunset until sunrise.
claims.statement_id: Mereka berbaris berkelompok di kegelapan malam sejak matahari terbenam hingga menjelang fajar.
claims.quote: They march in darkness after sunset and march as a group continuously until just before sunrise.

claims.statement: On the nights honoring the Hawaiian gods Kāne, Kū, Lono, or on the nights of Kanaloa, they are said to come forth from their burial sites or rise up from the ocean and march in a large group to ancient battle sites or other sacred places.
claims.statement_id: Pada malam yang menghormati dewa Hawaii Kāne, Kū, Lono, atau pada malam Kanaloa, mereka konon keluar dari makam atau muncul dari laut dan berbaris dalam rombongan besar menuju medan perang kuno atau tempat suci lain.
claims.quote: On the nights honoring the Hawaiian gods Kāne, Kū, Lono, or on the nights of Kanaloa, they are said to come forth from their burial sites or to rise up from the ocean, and to march in a large group to ancient Hawaiian battle sites or other sacred places.

claims.statement: The legend says the night marchers are normal-size warriors dressed for battle, carrying spears and clubs; some beat war drums and blow conch shells to announce their march.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, para pejalan malam adalah prajurit berukuran biasa yang berpakaian perang, membawa tombak dan pentungan; sebagian menabuh genderang perang dan meniup kerang untuk mengumumkan barisan mereka.
claims.quote: The legend says the night marchers are normal-size warriors, dressed for battle, carrying spears, clubs, and some are beating war drums and blowing tones from conch shells, to announce the advancing of their march.

claims.statement: According to the myth they are suspended in air; their feet touch neither water nor ground as they cross the night, and they leave no evidence of their visits.
claims.statement_id: Menurut mitos, mereka melayang di udara; kaki mereka tidak menyentuh air atau tanah saat melintasi malam, dan mereka tidak meninggalkan bukti kunjungan.
claims.quote: According to the myth, they are suspended in air; their feet do not touch water or ground as they traverse through the night, and they leave no evidence of their visitations.

claims.statement: According to ancient Hawaiian belief, any mortal who looks upon the marchers or is seen in defiance of them will die violently.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan Hawaii kuno, setiap manusia yang memandang atau terlihat melawan para pejalan itu akan mati secara kejam.
claims.quote: Ancient Hawaiian beliefs state that any mortal looking upon or being seen in defiance toward the marchers will die violently.

claims.statement: Some maintain that a mortal who lies motionless face down on the ground shows proper respect, fear and deference to the night marchers and will be spared.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang berpendapat bahwa manusia yang berbaring diam telungkup di tanah menunjukkan hormat, takut, dan tunduk kepada para pejalan malam sehingga akan dibiarkan.
claims.quote: Some people maintain that if the mortal lies motionless, face down on the ground, they are showing proper respect, fear, and deference to the night marchers, and they will be spared.

claims.statement: Mortals can also escape harm if an ancient ancestor among the marchers recognizes them; on meeting the mortal they call out "Naʻu!", meaning "mine" in Hawaiian.
claims.statement_id: Manusia juga dapat luput dari bahaya bila ada leluhur kuno di antara para pejalan yang mengenalinya; saat bertemu, mereka berseru "Naʻu!", yang berarti "milikku" dalam bahasa Hawaii.
claims.quote: Additionally, mortals can avoid harm or death from night marchers by being fortunate to have an ancient ancestor marcher present to recognize them. As they encounter the mortal, they will call out "Naʻu!", which means "mine" in Hawaiian.

claims.statement: Legend says planting living ti (Cordyline) shrubs around one's home keeps away all evil spirits and makes the huakaʻi pō avoid the area.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, menanam semak ti (Cordyline) hidup di sekeliling rumah menangkal semua roh jahat dan membuat huakaʻi pō menghindari daerah itu.
claims.quote: Legend says planting living ti (Cordyline sp.) shrubs around one's home is said to keep away all evil spirits and will cause the huakaʻi pō to avoid the area.

claims.statement: The signs are a foul, musky "death-like" odor and torches growing brighter as the night marchers draw closer.
claims.statement_id: Tanda-tandanya adalah bau apek dan busuk seperti kematian serta obor yang makin terang saat para pejalan malam mendekat.
claims.quote: The following signs are a foul and musky “death-like” odor, and torches getting brighter and brighter as the night marchers get closer.

claims.statement: Nightmarchers might appear during the day if they are to escort a dying relative to the spirit world.
claims.statement_id: Para pejalan malam bisa muncul pada siang hari bila mereka hendak mengantar kerabat yang sekarat ke dunia roh.
claims.quote: Nightmarchers might appear during the day if they are to escort a dying relative to the spirit world.

claims.statement: In ancient Hawaiian lore the body parts of a King or Chief were sacred and not to be seen by a mortal; the punishment for looking at them is always instant death, usually by bolts of intense light and flaming heat from several of the warrior's eyes aimed at the mortal.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Hawaii kuno, bagian tubuh raja atau kepala suku dinyatakan keramat dan tidak boleh dilihat manusia; hukuman bagi yang memandangnya selalu kematian seketika, biasanya oleh berkas cahaya dan panas menyala dari beberapa mata prajurit yang diarahkan kepada manusia itu.
claims.quote: In ancient Hawaiian lore, the laws declared body parts of a King or Chief to be sacred, and not to be seen by a mortal. The punishment for looking at these parts is always instant death, usually by bolts of intense light and flaming heat originating from several of the warrior's eyes aimed toward the mortal.

claims.statement: The goddess named Hiʻiaka-i-ka-poli-o-Pele (commonly shortened to Hiʻiaka) is often among the night marchers.
claims.statement_id: Dewi bernama Hiʻiaka-i-ka-poli-o-Pele (biasa disingkat Hiʻiaka) sering berada di antara para pejalan malam.
claims.quote: The Goddess named Hiʻiaka-i-ka-poli-o-Pele, (commonly shortened to Hiʻiaka), is often within the night marchers.

claims.statement: In the 2005 Lilo & Stitch: The Series episode "Belle", Lilo Pelekai seeks to prove Nightmarchers exist; they also feature in the 2021 Netflix film Finding ʻOhana.
claims.statement_id: Dalam episode "Belle" serial Lilo & Stitch: The Series (2005), Lilo Pelekai berusaha membuktikan bahwa Nightmarchers ada; Nightmarchers juga muncul dalam film Netflix Finding ʻOhana (2021).
claims.quote: In the 2005 Lilo & Stitch: The Series episode "Belle", Lilo Pelekai seeks to prove that Nightmarchers exist. Nightmarchers are also featured in the 2021 Netflix film Finding ʻOhana.

claims.statement: Processions of gods and spirits come on certain sacred nights to visit the sacred places or to welcome a dying relative and conduct him to the aumakua world.
claims.statement_id: Arak-arakan dewa dan roh datang pada malam-malam keramat tertentu untuk mengunjungi tempat suci atau menyambut kerabat yang sekarat dan menuntunnya ke dunia aumakua.
claims.quote: Especially is this true of the processions of gods and spirits who come on certain sacred nights to visit the sacred places, or to welcome a dying relative and conduct him to the aumakua world.

claims.statement: The processions are called "Marchers of the night" (Huakaʻi-pō) or "Spirit ranks" (Oiʻo).
claims.statement_id: Arak-arakan itu disebut "Pejalan malam" (Huakaʻi-pō) atau "Barisan roh" (Oiʻo).
claims.quote: "Marchers of the night" (Huaka‘i-po) or "Spirit ranks" (Oi‘o) they are called.

claims.statement: When seen, the marchers are always dressed in ancient fashion in the costume of chiefs or of gods; if the procession is one of gods, they move five abreast with five red torches between the ranks, accompanied only by chanting.
claims.statement_id: Bila terlihat, para pejalan selalu berpakaian ala adat kuno, yaitu busana kepala suku atau dewa; jika arak-arakan dewa, mereka berbaris lima sejajar dengan lima obor merah di antara barisan dan hanya diiringi nyanyian.
claims.quote: Always, if seen, the marchers are dressed according to ancient usage in the costume of chiefs or of gods. If the procession is one of gods, the marchers move five abreast with five torches burning red between the ranks, and without music save that of the voice raised in chant.

claims.statement: Processions of chiefs are accompanied by aumakua and march in silence or to the accompaniment of drum, nose-flute and chanting.
claims.statement_id: Arak-arakan kepala suku diiringi aumakua dan berjalan dalam diam atau diiringi genderang, seruling hidung, dan nyanyian.
claims.quote: Processions of chiefs are accompanied by aumakua and march in silence, or to the accompaniment of drum, nose-flute, and chanting.

claims.statement: They are seen on the sacred nights of Ku, Lono, Kane or Kanaloa, or by day if the procession welcomes the soul of a dying relative.
claims.statement_id: Mereka terlihat pada malam keramat Ku, Lono, Kane, atau Kanaloa, atau pada siang hari bila arak-arakan itu menyambut jiwa kerabat yang sekarat.
claims.quote: They are seen on the sacred nights of Ku, Lono, Kane, or Kanaloa, or they may be seen by day if it is a procession to welcome the soul of a dying relative.

claims.statement: Meeting such a procession is very dangerous: the leader cries "O-ia" ("Let him be pierced"), and if no dead relative or aumakua is present to protect him, a ghostly spearsman strikes him dead; the wise course is to "remove all clothing and turn face up and feign sleep".
claims.statement_id: Bertemu arak-arakan itu sangat berbahaya: pemimpinnya berseru "O-ia" ("Biarlah ia ditusuk"), dan bila tak ada kerabat di antara orang mati atau aumakuanya yang melindungi, seorang penombak hantu akan membunuhnya; yang bijak adalah "melepas semua pakaian dan telentang berpura-pura tidur".
claims.quote: To meet such a procession is very dangerous. "O-ia" (Let him be pierced) is the cry of the leader and if no relative among the dead or none of his aumakua is present to protect him, a ghostly spearsman will strike him dead. The wise thing to do is to "remove all clothing and turn face up and feign sleep."

claims.statement: Many Hawaiians, and even some persons of foreign blood, have seen this spirit march or heard the "chanting voices, the high notes of the flute, and drumming so loud as to seem beaten upon the side of the house".
claims.statement_id: Banyak orang Hawaii, bahkan beberapa orang berdarah asing, mengaku pernah melihat arak-arakan roh ini atau mendengar "suara orang bernyanyi, nada tinggi seruling, dan tabuhan yang begitu keras seolah dipukul di dinding rumah".
claims.quote: Many Hawaiians and even some persons of foreign blood have seen this spirit march or heard the "chanting voices, the high notes of the flute, and drumming so loud as to seem beaten upon the side of the house."

claims.statement: High chiefs and warriors are supposed to march in crowds carrying spears and piercing those they met, unless some ghost recognized the person and called "Alia [wait]"; if the word was "O-i-o [throw the spear]!" that spirit's spear brought death to the passer-by.
claims.statement_id: Kepala suku tinggi dan prajurit konon berbaris berbondong-bondong membawa tombak dan menusuk orang yang mereka temui, kecuali ada hantu yang mengenali orang itu dan berseru "Alia [tunggu]"; bila yang diserukan "O-i-o [lemparkan tombak]!", tombak roh itu membawa kematian bagi si pejalan.
claims.quote: The high chiefs and warriors are supposed to march and go in crowds, carrying their spears and piercing those they met unless some ghost recognized that one and called to the others, "Alia [wait]," but if the word was "O-i-o [throw the spear]!" then that spirit's spear would strike death to the passer-by.

claims.statement: Barriers placed in the path of night marchers will not deter them.
claims.statement_id: Rintangan yang dipasang di jalur para pejalan malam tidak akan menghalangi mereka.
claims.quote: Barriers placed in the path of night marchers will not deter them.

claims.statement: The Queensland tiger is a creature in Australian folklore reputed to inhabit Queensland.
claims.statement_id: Queensland tiger adalah makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Australia yang konon hidup di Queensland.
claims.quote: In Australian folklore, the Queensland tiger is a creature said to live in the Queensland area in eastern Australia.

claims.statement: Known as yarri, it is described as a dog-sized striped feline with violent temperament.
claims.statement_id: Dikenal sebagai yarri, makhluk ini digambarkan seperti kucing berukuran anjing dengan loreng dan sifat buas.
claims.quote: Also known by the Indigenous name yarri, it is described as being a dog-sized feline with stripes, a long tail, prominent front teeth, and a violent temperament.

claims.statement: It has been hypothesized as a survivor or descendant of the predatory marsupial Thylacoleo.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini dihipotesiskan sebagai keturunan atau penyintas dari predator marsupial purba Thylacoleo.
claims.quote: It has been hypothesized to be a survivor or descendant of the large predatory marsupial Thylacoleo, officially considered to be extinct, or possibly a large feral cat variant (given possible discrepancies with Thylacoleo dentition).

claims.statement: The earliest documented witness reports of a Queensland marsupial tiger date from 1871, with Indigenous traditions of the yarri preceding them.
claims.statement_id: Laporan saksi paling awal yang terdokumentasi tentang harimau berkantung Queensland berasal dari 1871, dan tradisi Pribumi tentang yarri mendahuluinya.
claims.quote: The earliest documented witness reports of a Queensland marsupial tiger date from 1871, with Indigenous traditions of the yarri preceding these.

claims.statement: In 1926, A. S. le Souef described a "Striped marsupial cat" in The Wild Animals of Australasia.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1926, A. S. le Souef menggambarkan "kucing berkantung bergaris" dalam The Wild Animals of Australasia.
claims.quote: In 1926, A. S. le Souef described a "Striped marsupial cat" in The Wild Animals of Australasia,

claims.statement: In his 1965 revision of Furred Animals of Australia, Ellis Troughton proposed that the Queensland tiger was in fact a mainland variant of the thylacine.
claims.statement_id: Dalam revisi 1965 buku Furred Animals of Australia, Ellis Troughton mengusulkan bahwa harimau Queensland sebenarnya varian daratan dari thylacine.
claims.quote: In his 1965 revision of the book Furred Animals of Australia, Ellis Troughton proposed that the Queensland tiger was, in actuality, a mainland variant of the thylacine.

claims.statement: Modern sightings, when investigated, have always been narrowed down to introduced feral cats.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan modern, bila diselidiki, selalu dipersempit menjadi kucing liar yang didatangkan.
claims.quote: Modern sightings, when investigated, have been universally narrowed down to introduced feral cats.

claims.statement: Bob Whiston and tree-kangaroo expert Roger Martin suggest that sightings are of Lumholtz's or Bennett's tree-kangaroos, lesser-known animals that walk on four legs on the ground and live in regions where Queensland tiger reports originate.
claims.statement_id: Bob Whiston dan pakar kanguru pohon Roger Martin menyarankan bahwa penampakan itu adalah kanguru pohon Lumholtz atau Bennett, hewan kurang dikenal yang berjalan empat kaki di tanah dan hidup di wilayah asal laporan harimau Queensland.
claims.quote: with local Bob Whiston and tree-kangaroo expert Roger Martin suggesting that sightings are either of Lumholtz's or Bennett's tree-kangaroos, less-well-known animals that walk on four legs when terrestrial and which are found in regions where Queensland tiger reports originate.

claims.statement: Theories of continued Thylacoleo presence on mainland Australia and thylacine survival in Tasmania have been covered in television shows on the National Geographic Channel and on Animal Planet's Animal X.
claims.statement_id: Teori bahwa Thylacoleo masih ada di daratan Australia dan thylacine bertahan di Tasmania pernah diulas dalam berbagai acara televisi di National Geographic Channel dan Animal X milik Animal Planet.
claims.quote: The theories of continued Thylacoleo presence on mainland Australia and thylacine survival in Tasmania have been covered in various television shows on the National Geographic Channel and also on Animal Planet's Animal X.

claims.statement: In the 1970s naturalist Janeice Plunkett collected over 100 reports of sightings or shootings of "tigers", including accounts alleging that the animal was a marsupial.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1970-an, naturalis Janeice Plunkett mengumpulkan lebih dari 100 laporan penampakan atau penembakan "harimau", termasuk kisah yang menyebut hewan itu berkantung.
claims.quote: In the 1970s, naturalist Janeice Plunkett collected over 100 reports of sightings or shootings of "tigers", including accounts alleging that the animal observed was a marsupial.

claims.statement: On the summit of the Coast Mountains lived two varieties of mammals that seemed unknown to science; one they called yarri, which from their description the author took to be a marsupial tiger.
claims.statement_id: Di puncak Pegunungan Pantai hidup dua jenis mamalia yang tampak belum dikenal ilmu pengetahuan; salah satunya mereka sebut yarri, dan dari gambaran mereka pengarang menyimpulkannya sebagai harimau berkantung.
claims.quote: on the summit of the Coast Mountains, before mentioned, there lived two varieties of mammals which seemed to me to be unknown to science ... One of the animals they called yarri. From their description I conceived it to be a marsupial tiger.

claims.statement: The yarri was said to be about the size of a dingo, with shorter legs and a long tail, and was described by the blacks as very savage.
claims.statement_id: Yarri disebut seukuran dingo, dengan kaki lebih pendek dan ekor panjang, dan digambarkan oleh penduduk Aborigin sebagai sangat ganas.
claims.quote: It was said to be about the size of a dingo, though its legs were shorter and its tail long, and it was described by the blacks as being very savage.

claims.statement: If pursued the yarri climbed trees where the natives dared not follow, and they showed by gestures how it would growl and bite their hands.
claims.statement_id: Bila dikejar, yarri memanjat pohon tempat penduduk tidak berani mengikutinya; mereka memperagakan bagaimana ia menggeram dan menggigit tangan mereka.
claims.quote: If pursued it climbed up the trees, where the natives did not dare follow it, and by gestures they explained to me how at such times it would growl and bite their hands.

claims.statement: Rocky retreats were its favourite habitat, and its principal food was said to be a little brown variety of wallaby common in Northern Queensland scrubs.
claims.statement_id: Tempat berlindung berbatu adalah habitat favoritnya, dan makanan utamanya konon sejenis wallaby cokelat kecil yang umum di semak Queensland utara.
claims.quote: Rocky retreats were its most favourite habitat, and its principal food was said to be a little brown variety of wallaby common in Northern Queensland scrubs.

claims.statement: Its flesh was not particularly appreciated by the blacks, and if they accidentally killed a yarri they gave it to their old women.
claims.statement_id: Dagingnya tidak terlalu disukai penduduk Aborigin, dan bila tak sengaja membunuh yarri mereka memberikannya kepada para perempuan tua.
claims.quote: Its flesh was not particularly appreciated by the blacks, and if they accidentally killed a yarri they gave it to their old women.

claims.statement: In Western Queensland the author heard much about an animal that seemed identical with the yarri, and a specimen was once nearly shot.
claims.statement_id: Di Queensland Barat pengarang banyak mendengar tentang hewan yang tampaknya identik dengan yarri, dan seekor spesimen pernah nyaris tertembak.
claims.quote: In Western Queensland I heard much about an animal which seemed to me to be identical with the yarri here described, and a specimen was once nearly shot

claims.statement: The natives had a superstition that "a great water will rise" if a young man picks up a dead yarri.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk punya takhayul bahwa "air besar akan naik" bila seorang pemuda memungut yarri yang mati.
claims.quote: The natives having a superstition that " a great water will rise " if a young man picks up a dead yarri,

claims.statement: The author obtained a young yarri that he identified as Dasyurus maculatus, and wrote that yarri is a name applied to a whole family.
claims.statement_id: Pengarang memperoleh seekor yarri muda yang ia kenali sebagai Dasyurus maculatus, dan menulis bahwa yarri adalah nama yang dipakai untuk seluruh satu famili.
claims.quote: YARRI [Dasyurus maculatus). ... yarri being a name applied to the whole family of Dasyiiridce.

claims.statement: The author was nevertheless convinced that a large animal of this kind exists that has not yet been discovered.
claims.statement_id: Namun pengarang yakin masih ada hewan besar sejenis itu yang belum ditemukan.
claims.quote: I am, however, convinced that there exists a large animal of this kind that has not yet been discovered.

claims.statement: Ukupanipo is a Hawaiian shark god who controls the amount of fish available to fishermen.
claims.statement_id: Ukupanipo adalah dewa hiu Hawaii yang mengatur keberadaan ikan agar dapat ditangkap nelayan.
claims.quote: In Hawaiian mythology, Ukupanipo is a shark god who controls the amount of fish close enough for the fisherman to catch.

claims.statement: He occasionally adopts human children who gain shark-shifting powers and bear a shark mark.
claims.statement_id: Ia terkadang mengadopsi anak manusia yang memperoleh kekuatan berubah menjadi hiu dan bertanda khusus di pundak.
claims.quote: He occasionally adopts a human child who gains the power to transform into a shark, but when in human form has a mark like a shark's mouth under their shoulder blades.

claims.statement: The favour of the sea was invoked through Ukupanipo, the shark-god, who with his followers could drive the fish to or from the shores, giving or withholding the native's daily food.
claims.statement_id: Karunia laut diminta melalui Ukupanipo, dewa hiu, yang bersama pengikutnya dapat menggiring ikan mendekat atau menjauh dari pantai, memberi atau menahan makanan sehari-hari penduduk.
claims.quote: it was invoked through Uku- panipo, the shark-god, who, with his followers, could drive the fish to or from the shores, giving or withholding the daily food of the native.

claims.statement: Ukupanipo is credited with occasionally adopting a human child, to whom he gives the favour of the sea and who can change into a shark at will.
claims.statement_id: Ukupanipo dipercaya sesekali mengangkat anak manusia, yang ia beri karunia laut dan yang mampu berubah menjadi hiu sesuka hati.
claims.quote: Ukupanipo is credited with occasionally adopting a human child, to whom he gives the favour of the sea, and who has the ability to change into a shark at will.

claims.statement: These sea-children possess the ravenous mien and dangerous temper of the god.
claims.statement_id: Anak-anak laut itu memiliki raut rakus dan watak berbahaya seperti sang dewa.
claims.quote: These sea-children possess the ravenous mien and dangerous temper of the god.

claims.statement: The mark Ukupanipo places upon them is a mouth-like orifice, garnished with teeth, below the shoulder-blades.
claims.statement_id: Tanda yang diberikan Ukupanipo pada mereka adalah lubang menyerupai mulut berbaris gigi di bawah tulang belikat.
claims.quote: The mark which Ukupanipo places upon them is a mouth-like orifice below the shoulder-blades, garnished with teeth.

claims.statement: Adaro is a term for two distinct classes of beings in Makira mythology in the Solomon Islands.
claims.statement_id: Adaro adalah istilah untuk dua kelas entitas dalam mitologi pulau Makira di Kepulauan Solomon.
claims.quote: Adaro is a term for two distinct classes of beings found in the mythology of Makira island, in the Solomon Islands.

claims.statement: The word adaro comes from Arosi, meaning corpse, ghost, soul, or spirit.
claims.statement_id: Kata adaro berasal dari bahasa Arosi dengan makna antara lain mayat, hantu, jiwa, atau roh.
claims.quote: The word adaro is from the Arosi language; it has several meanings, including 'corpse; ghost; soul; spirit'.

claims.statement: Adaro most often inhabit sharks or other marine creatures.
claims.statement_id: Adaro paling sering merasuki hiu atau hewan-hewan laut lainnya.
claims.quote: Adaro (ghosts) most often enter into sharks or other marine animals.

claims.statement: The aunga passes from this world after death, while the adaro remains.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, aunga meninggalkan dunia ini setelah kematian, sedangkan adaro tetap tinggal.
claims.quote: The aunga passes from this world after death, while the adaro remains.

claims.statement: There is an adaro who guards and an adaro who rules the Rotomana, the place where the aunga go upon death.
claims.statement_id: Ada adaro yang menjaga dan adaro yang memerintah Rotomana, tempat aunga pergi setelah kematian.
claims.quote: There is an adaro who guards and an adaro who rules the Rotomana, the place where the aunga go upon death.

claims.statement: According to Fox, one great class of adaro consists of ghosts, and it is these chiefly that are worshipped.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Fox, satu golongan besar adaro adalah arwah orang mati, dan inilah yang terutama disembah.
claims.quote: One great class of adaro consists therefore of ghosts, and it is these chiefly that are worshipped.

claims.statement: According to Fox, a second class are spirits of the sea, woods and shore, and others found in the rainbow and the waterspout; in native opinion these are not ghosts.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Fox, golongan kedua adalah roh laut, hutan, dan pantai, serta roh pelangi dan pusaran air; menurut penduduk setempat mereka bukan arwah orang mati.
claims.quote: spirits of the sea, woods, and shore, and others found in the rainbow and the waterspout. These are not ghosts, in native opinion, whatever their origin may have been.

claims.statement: These ghost sharks did not harm their worshippers but were often sent by them to kill men at a distance.
claims.statement_id: Hiu-hiu arwah ini tidak mencelakai para penyembahnya, tetapi sering dikirim mereka untuk membunuh orang dari jauh.
claims.quote: These ghost sharks did not harm their worshippers, but were often sent by them to kill men at a distance.

claims.statement: Sea spirits are represented as partly human, partly fish-like, and are thought to live far out to sea or near small islands along the coast.
claims.statement_id: Roh laut digambarkan setengah manusia, setengah ikan, dan dipercaya tinggal jauh di tengah laut atau dekat pulau-pulau kecil di sepanjang pantai.
claims.quote: They are represented as partly human, partly fish-like. They are thought to live far out to sea or near small islands along the coast.

claims.statement: Adaro ni matawa, the sea spirits, are malevolent beings that shoot men with flying-fish.
claims.statement_id: Adaro ni matawa (roh laut) adalah makhluk jahat yang menembak manusia dengan ikan terbang.
claims.quote: Adaro ni matawa are malevolent beings. They shoot men with flying-fish.

claims.statement: Atanua is the goddess of dawn in Marquesan Polynesian mythology and wife of Atea.
claims.statement_id: Atanua adalah dewi fajar dalam mitologi Polinesia di Kepulauan Marquesas dan istri dari Atea.
claims.quote: Atanua (or Atanea) in Polynesian mythology (specifically: the Marquesas Islands) is the goddess of the dawn and wife of Atea

claims.statement: Their son is the first human, named Tu-Mea.
claims.statement_id: Putra Atanua adalah manusia pertama yang bernama Tu-Mea.
claims.quote: Their son is the first man, Tu-Mea.

claims.statement: She created the seas after a miscarriage that filled the oceans with amniotic fluid.
claims.statement_id: Atanua menciptakan lautan setelah mengalami keguguran yang memenuhi samudra.
claims.quote: She created the seas after having a miscarriage and filling the oceans with her amniotic fluid.

claims.statement: According to Handy, in house-building chants Atanua is called wife of Atea and ancestress of all men.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Handy, dalam nyanyian pembangunan rumah Atanua disebut istri Atea dan leluhur perempuan semua manusia.
claims.quote: of the house of Atanua, wife of Atea and ancestress of all men.

claims.statement: According to Handy, the platform of the original fa'e Papa, where Atanua the ancestress of the Marquesas islanders lived, is said to lie under the sea a little way from the western end of the beach at Atu Ona.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Handy, landasan (paepae) fa'e Papa asli, tempat tinggal Atanua leluhur penduduk Marquesas, dikatakan terletak di bawah laut tidak jauh dari ujung barat pantai Atu Ona.
claims.quote: in which lived Atanua, the ancestress of the Marquesas islanders, lies under the sea a little way from the westward end of the beach at Atu Ona.

claims.statement: According to Handy, genealogies usually start with the names Atea and Atanua, regarded as progenitor and progenitress of the native people.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Handy, silsilah biasanya dimulai dengan nama Atea dan Atanua, yang dianggap sebagai leluhur laki-laki dan perempuan penduduk asli.
claims.quote: Genealogies usually start with these names, these two being regarded as, respectively, progenitor and progenitress of the native people.

claims.statement: According to Handy, modern natives explain that Atea and Atanua are like Adam and Eve.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Handy, penduduk asli masa kini menjelaskan bahwa Atea dan Atanua seperti Adam dan Hawa.
claims.quote: Modern natives, in explaining the matter, say that Atea and Atanua are like Adam and Eve.

claims.statement: Handy judges that Atea and Atanua were distinctly deities rather than human beings, with nothing to indicate that they were conceived as ever living on the islands in human form.
claims.statement_id: Handy menilai bahwa Atea dan Atanua jelas adalah dewa, bukan manusia, dan tidak ada petunjuk bahwa mereka pernah dibayangkan mendiami pulau-pulau itu dalam wujud manusia.
claims.quote: for Atea and Atanua were distinctly deities rather than human beings, and there is nothing to indicate that they are conceived of as having ever inhabited the islands as beings in human form.

claims.statement: In Hawaiian mythology, an ʻaumakua is a personal or family god that originated as a deified ancestor.
claims.statement_id: ʻAumakua adalah dewa pribadi atau keluarga dalam mitologi Hawaii yang berasal dari leluhur yang didewakan.
claims.quote: is a personal or family god that originated as a deified ancestor, and which takes on physical forms such as spirit vehicles.

claims.statement: An ʻaumakua can manifest as a shark, owl, bird, octopus, or inanimate objects.
claims.statement_id: ʻAumakua dapat menampakkan wujud sebagai hiu, burung hantu, burung, gurita, atau benda mati.
claims.quote: An ʻaumakua may manifest as a shark, owl, bird, octopus, or inanimate objects such as plants or rocks.

claims.statement: ʻAumākua were believed to watch over their families and hear their words, give them strength and guidance, warn them of misfortune or danger, and punish wrong-doers.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan, ʻaumākua mengawasi keluarga mereka dan mendengar kata-kata mereka, memberi kekuatan dan bimbingan, memperingatkan akan kemalangan atau bahaya, serta menghukum pelaku kesalahan.
claims.quote: ʻAumākua were believed to watch over their families and hear their words, give them strength and guidance, warn them of misfortune or danger, give punishments to wrong-doers

claims.statement: ʻAumākua could also bring punishment to families who offended or displeased them.
claims.statement_id: ʻAumākua juga dapat menghukum keluarga yang menyinggung atau tidak menyenangkan mereka.
claims.quote: ʻAumākua could also bring punishment to families who offended or displeased them.

claims.statement: ʻAumākua were able to take on kino lau (many bodies, many forms).
claims.statement_id: ʻAumākua dapat mengambil kino lau (banyak tubuh, banyak wujud).
claims.quote: ʻAumākua were able to take on kino lau (many bodies, many forms)

claims.statement: A note to Malo's text says that, in general, an aumakua was an ancestral deity whose worship and mutual service was handed down from father to son.
claims.statement_id: Dalam catatan penerjemah Malo, secara umum aumakua adalah dewa leluhur yang pemujaan dan pelayanan timbal baliknya diwariskan dari ayah kepada anak.
claims.quote: In general an aumakua was an ancestral deity, whose worship and mutual service was handed down from father to son.

claims.statement: The note names Ku, Kane, Kanaloa and Lono as aumakuas, as were many lesser gods, and says a man might have several aumakuas.
claims.statement_id: Catatan itu menyebut Ku, Kane, Kanaloa, dan Lono sebagai aumakua, demikian pula banyak dewa yang lebih kecil, dan seseorang boleh memiliki beberapa aumakua.
claims.quote: Ku, Kane, Kanaloa and Lono were aumakuas, as were a host of lesser gods. A man might have several aumakuas.

claims.statement: Daucina is the great god of seafaring in Fijian mythology.
claims.statement_id: Daucina adalah dewa pelayaran laut agung dalam mitologi Fiji.
claims.quote: In Fijian mythology (Fiji), Daucina ("torchbearer") is the great god of seafaring Fiji.

claims.statement: As a toddler Daucina was only quiet when looking at a lamp.
claims.statement_id: Semasa balita Daucina hanya diam ketika menatap lampu.
claims.quote: When Daucina was a toddler, he was only quiet when looking at a lamp.

claims.statement: His mother tied fiery reeds to his head to keep him calm.
claims.statement_id: Ibunya mengikatkan alang-alang berapi di kepalanya agar ia tenang.
claims.quote: His mother tied fiery reeds to his head so that he would be calm.

claims.statement: Thomson writes that next after Ndengei comes Ndauthina (the torch-bearer), the god of the seafaring and fishing community throughout Fiji.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Thomson, setelah Ndengei, Ndauthina (sang pembawa obor) adalah dewa komunitas pelaut dan nelayan di seluruh Fiji.
claims.quote: Next in order to Ndengei is Ndauthina (the torch-bearer), the god of the seafaring and fishing community throughout Fiji.

claims.statement: Thomson records that his love of light in infancy led his mother to bind lighted reeds on his head, and that he now roams the reefs by night hooded with a flaming brazier.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Thomson, karena cintanya pada cahaya sejak bayi, ibunya mengikatkan alang-alang bernyala di kepalanya, dan kini ia berkeliaran di terumbu pada malam hari berkerudung tungku menyala.
claims.quote: His love of light in infancy prompted his mother to bind lighted reeds upon his head to amuse him, and now he roams the reefs by night hooded with a flaming brazier.

claims.statement: Thomson records that he is the patron of adulterers and himself steals women away by night.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Thomson, ia adalah pelindung para pezina dan sendiri membawa pergi perempuan pada malam hari.
claims.quote: He is the patron of adulterers, and himself steals women away by night.

claims.statement: Thomson records that he loves night attacks and flashes light on the defences to guide the besiegers.
claims.statement_id: Thomson mencatat bahwa ia menyukai serangan malam dan menyorotkan cahaya ke pertahanan untuk memandu para pengepung.
claims.quote: He loves night attacks, and flashes light upon the defences to guide the besiegers.

claims.statement: Thomson records that upon his friends the fishermen he plays no pranks, giving them fair winds and good fishing.
claims.statement_id: Thomson mencatat bahwa terhadap para nelayan sahabatnya ia tidak berbuat jahil, malah memberi angin baik dan hasil tangkapan yang bagus.
claims.quote: But upon his friends the fishermen he plays no pranks, giving them fair winds and good fishing.

claims.statement: According to Thomson, a shipwrecked fisherman might always find sanctuary in a temple dedicated to Ndauthina.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Thomson, nelayan yang karam selalu dapat menemukan perlindungan di kuil yang dipersembahkan kepada Ndauthina.
claims.quote: But the shipwrecked fisherman might always find sanctuary in a temple dedicated to Ndauthina

claims.statement: Williams records that Ndauthina steals women of rank and beauty by night or torch-light.
claims.statement_id: Williams mencatat bahwa Ndauthina mencuri perempuan bangsawan dan cantik pada malam hari atau dengan cahaya obor.
claims.quote: Ndauthina steals women of rank and beauty by night or torch-light.

claims.statement: Flaming Teeth was a giant in Fijian lore whose teeth looked like burning logs.
claims.statement_id: Flaming Teeth adalah raksasa dalam mitologi Fiji yang bertubuh begitu besar hingga giginya tampak seperti kayu membara.
claims.quote: Flaming Teeth, from Fijian mythology, was a giant who was so large his teeth appeared as burning logs.

claims.statement: The colossal monster terrorized villages by eating people and causing wide damage.
claims.statement_id: Raksasa ini meneror desa-desa dengan memangsa manusia dan membawa kehancuran.
claims.quote: The colossal creature terrorized villages relentlessly, devouring people and causing widespread destruction.

claims.statement: After enduring countless attacks and losses, a group of courageous villagers banded together.
claims.statement_id: Setelah menanggung serangan dan kerugian yang tak terhitung, sekelompok penduduk desa yang berani bersatu.
claims.quote: After enduring countless attacks and losses, a group of courageous villagers banded together.

claims.statement: They devised a strategy to ambush the giant, luring it beneath a massive rock and delivering a fatal blow to its skull.
claims.statement_id: Mereka menyusun siasat menyergap raksasa itu dengan memancingnya ke bawah batu besar dan menghantam tengkoraknya hingga tewas.
claims.quote: They devised a strategy to ambush the giant, enticing it beneath a massive rock and delivering a fatal blow to its skull.

claims.statement: They succeeded in killing the giant, but its teeth were still aflame.
claims.statement_id: Mereka berhasil membunuh raksasa itu, tetapi giginya masih menyala.
claims.quote: They succeeded killing the giant but its teeth still were aflame.

claims.statement: The villagers took the teeth back to the village, and that was the first time man acquired the use of fire.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk desa membawa gigi itu ke desa, dan itulah pertama kalinya manusia memperoleh penggunaan api.
claims.quote: The villagers took the teeth back to the village and that was the first time man acquired the use of fire.

claims.statement: Płonącozęby ("Flaming Teeth") is a giant in Fijian mythology; according to the beliefs of the people of the Fiji islands his characteristic feature was huge flaming teeth.
claims.statement_id: Płonącozęby ("Gigi Berapi") adalah raksasa dalam mitologi Fiji; menurut kepercayaan penduduk kepulauan Fiji, ciri khasnya adalah gigi besar yang menyala.
claims.quote: Płonącozęby – olbrzym występujący mitologii fidżyjskiej. Według wierzeń mieszkańców wysp Fidżi, jego cechą charakterystyczną były ogromne płonące zęby.

claims.statement: Płonącozęby was lured beneath an enormous rock, which was then dropped onto his head, crushing his skull.
claims.statement_id: Płonącozęby dipancing ke bawah batu raksasa, lalu batu itu dijatuhkan ke kepalanya sehingga menghancurkan tengkoraknya.
claims.quote: Płonącozęby został zwabiony pod ogromną skałę, którą następnie zrzucili mu na głowę, miażdżąc czaszkę.

claims.statement: After the giant's death the villagers took his flaming teeth back to the village, and from then on people learned to use fire.
claims.statement_id: Setelah raksasa itu mati, penduduk desa membawa gigi apinya kembali ke desa, dan sejak itu manusia belajar menggunakan api.
claims.quote: Po śmierci olbrzyma wieśniacy zabrali jego płonące zęby z powrotem do wioski, od tego czasu ludzie nauczyli się używać ognia.

claims.statement: In Australian Aboriginal mythology, Galeru or Galaru is a rainbow serpent.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Aborigin Australia, Galeru atau Galaru adalah seekor ular pelangi.
claims.quote: Dans la mythologie des Aborigènes d'Australie, Galeru (ou Galaru) est un serpent arc-en-ciel

claims.statement: Galeru symbolizes the continuation of life on Earth.
claims.statement_id: Galeru melambangkan kelangsungan hidup di Bumi.
claims.quote: Il symbolise la continuation de la vie sur Terre.

claims.statement: The Rainbow Serpent is a common creator deity known under many names across Aboriginal languages.
claims.statement_id: Ular Pelangi adalah dewa umum yang dipandang sebagai dewa pencipta dalam masyarakat Aborigin Australia.
claims.quote: The Rainbow Serpent or Rainbow Snake is a common deity, often seen as the creator god, known by numerous names in different Australian Aboriginal languages by the many different Aboriginal peoples.

claims.statement: In the list of names for the Rainbow Serpent, Galeru (or Galoru, Kaleru) is attributed to the Wandjina of the Kimberley Region.
claims.statement_id: Dalam daftar nama Ular Pelangi, Galeru (atau Galoru, Kaleru) dikaitkan dengan Wandjina di wilayah Kimberley.
claims.quote: Galeru (or Galoru, Kaleru) by the Wandjina (Kimberley Region)

claims.statement: A Wikipedia list describes Galeru as a rainbow snake in Arnhem Land mythology who swallowed the Djanggawul.
claims.statement_id: Daftar Wikipedia menyebut Galeru sebagai ular pelangi dalam mitologi Arnhem Land yang menelan Djanggawul.
claims.quote: Galeru, rainbow snake in Arnhem Land mythology who swallowed the Djanggawul

claims.statement: In general terms, the Rainbow Serpent creates land and diversity for Aboriginal people but can bring great chaos when disturbed.
claims.statement_id: Secara umum, Ular Pelangi menciptakan tanah dan keragaman bagi orang Aborigin, tetapi bila diganggu dapat membawa kekacauan besar.
claims.quote: Much like the archetypal mother goddess, the Rainbow Serpent creates land and diversity for the Aboriginal people, but when disturbed can bring great chaos.

claims.statement: According to Berndt citing Kaberry, in northeastern Kimberley the Rainbow Snake known as Galeru (Kaleru) is a life saver and sustainer, the embodiment of fertility.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Berndt yang merujuk Kaberry, di Kimberley timur laut Ular Pelangi bernama Galeru (Kaleru) adalah penyelamat dan penopang hidup, perwujudan kesuburan.
claims.quote: According to Phyllis M. Kaberry, in northeastern Kimberley, the Rainbow Snake known as Galeru (Kaleru) is also a life saver and sustainer, the embodiment of fertility

claims.statement: According to Berndt, he is a lawgiver responsible for features of social organization such as marriage rules and subsections.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Berndt, ia adalah pemberi hukum, yang bertanggung jawab atas ciri organisasi sosial seperti aturan perkawinan dan subseksi.
claims.quote: He is a lawgiver, responsible for such features of social organization as marriage rules and subsections

claims.statement: According to Berndt, pearl shells come from him, and in some circumstances it is dangerous to dream of them.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Berndt, kerang mutiara berasal darinya, dan dalam keadaan tertentu berbahaya memimpikannya.
claims.quote: Pearl shells come from him, and in some circumstances it is dangerous to dream of them

claims.statement: In Hawaiian religion, Kamohoaliʻi is a shark and steam god and sibling of Pele and Nāmaka.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan Hawaii, Kamohoaliʻi adalah dewa hiu dan uap serta saudara dari Pele dan Nāmaka.
claims.quote: In Hawaiian religion, Kamohoaliʻi (also Ka-moho-ali’i or Moho) is a shark and steam god and a brother of Kāne Milohaʻi, Pele, Kapo, Nāmaka, and Hiʻiaka.

claims.statement: Kamohoaliʻi swam in waters around Maui and Kahoʻolawe.
claims.statement_id: Kamohoaliʻi berenang di kawasan perairan sekitar pulau Maui dan Kahoʻolawe.
claims.quote: Kamohoaliʻi swam in the area around the islands of Maui and Kahoʻolawe.

claims.statement: When a ship was lost, Kamohoaliʻi shook his tail to guide sailors home after kahuna fed him awa.
claims.statement_id: Saat kapal tersesat di samudra, Kamohoaliʻi mengibaskan ekornya memandu pelaut pulang setelah diberi minum awa.
claims.quote: When a ship was lost at sea, Ka-moho-aliʻi shook his tail in front of the fleet and the kahuna would feed him awa, a narcotic drink, and Kamohoaliʻi would guide the men home.

claims.statement: Westervelt records that Ka-moho-alii, whose name was sometimes given as Ka-moo-alii, was king of the sharks.
claims.statement_id: Westervelt mencatat bahwa Ka-moho-alii, yang namanya kadang ditulis Ka-moo-alii, adalah raja para hiu.
claims.quote: Ka-moho-alii, whose name was sometimes given as Ka-moo-alii, was king of the sharks.

claims.statement: Westervelt writes that Ka-moho-alii, the shark-god, was the elder brother and the caretaker of the family.
claims.statement_id: Westervelt menulis bahwa Ka-moho-alii, sang dewa hiu, adalah kakak tertua dan penjaga keluarga.
claims.quote: Ka-moho-alii, the shark-god, ... He was the elder brother, the caretaker of the family.

claims.statement: Westervelt relates that Ka-moho-alii provided the great boat Honua-i-a-kea (The great spread-out world) and carried the family away to distant islands.
claims.statement_id: Westervelt menceritakan bahwa Ka-moho-alii menyediakan perahu besar Honua-i-a-kea (Dunia yang terbentang luas) dan membawa keluarga itu ke pulau-pulau yang jauh.
claims.quote: There Ka-moho-alii provided them with the great boat Honua-i-a-kea (The great spread-out world) and carried them away to distant islands.

claims.statement: Westervelt records that sometimes Pele's brother Kamohoalii, the great shark-god, in the form of a shark would be her surf-board.
claims.statement_id: Westervelt mencatat bahwa kadang-kadang saudaranya Kamohoalii, dewa hiu agung, berwujud hiu menjadi papan selancar Pele.
claims.quote: Sometimes her brother, Kamohoalii, the great shark-god, in the form of a shark would be her surf-board.

claims.statement: Emerson notes that he was the brother of Pele and in one metamorphosis took the form of a shark.
claims.statement_id: Emerson mencatat bahwa ia saudara Pele dan dalam satu perubahan wujud ia berbentuk hiu.
claims.quote: The brother of Pele ; in one metamorphosis he took the form of a shark.

claims.statement: Emerson notes that a high point in the northwest quarter of the wall of Kilauea was considered his special residence and so sacred that no smoke or flame from the volcano ever touched it.
claims.statement_id: Emerson mencatat bahwa sebuah titik tinggi di sisi barat laut dinding Kilauea dianggap sebagai tempat tinggal khususnya dan begitu keramat sehingga asap atau api gunung itu tidak pernah menyentuhnya.
claims.quote: A high point in the northwest quarter of the wall of Kilauea was considered his special residence and regarded as so sacred that no smoke or flame from the volcano ever touched it.

claims.statement: The moehau is a creature in New Zealand folklore reputed to live on Coromandel Peninsula's Moehau.
claims.statement_id: Moehau adalah makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Selandia Baru yang konon mendiami Moehau di Semenanjung Coromandel.
claims.quote: In New Zealand folklore, the moehau (also called the maeroero) is a creature said to dwell in the Coromandel Peninsula's Moehau of New Zealand's North Island.

claims.statement: Some Māori suggest it descends from maero wild men, while another theory posited an escaped baboon.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang Māori memandangnya keturunan maero, sedangkan dugaan lain menduganya kera yang kabur.
claims.quote: Some Māori people suggest that the creature is a descendant of the maero (sometimes described as giants or wild men of the woods), but another explanation for the moehau is that it was an exaggerated report of an escaped gorilla or baboon.

claims.statement: In 1970 County Councillor Jim Reedy told Robyn Gosset that the Hairy Moehau was an exaggeration that started from a joke.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1970 anggota dewan daerah Jim Reedy mengatakan kepada Robyn Gosset bahwa Moehau Berbulu adalah pembesar-besaran yang bermula dari lelucon.
claims.quote: However, in 1970, County Councillor Jim Reedy told Robyn Gosset that the Hairy Moehau was an exaggeration started from a joke.

claims.statement: George Dean, Director of Auckland Zoo, refuted the baboon theory.
claims.statement_id: George Dean, Direktur Kebun Binatang Auckland, membantah teori babon.
claims.quote: George Dean, Director of Auckland Zoo, refuted the baboon theory

claims.statement: In 1970 Bob Grey told researcher Robyn Gosset that the term Moehau Monster came from a name given to a Yankee steam hauler used for logging.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1970 Bob Grey mengatakan kepada peneliti Robyn Gosset bahwa istilah Moehau Monster berasal dari nama yang diberikan kepada sebuah Yankee steam hauler yang dipakai untuk menebang kayu.
claims.quote: Also in 1970, Bob Grey told researcher Robyn Gosset that the term Moehau Monster came from a name given to a Yankee steam hauler that was utilized for logging.

claims.statement: In Māori tradition the Maero (or Mohoao) are an iwi-atua, a supernatural people of New Zealand.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Māori, Maero (atau Mohoao) adalah iwi-atua, bangsa supernatural dari Selandia Baru.
claims.quote: In Māori tradition, the Maero (or Mohoao) are an iwi-atua or supernatural people from New Zealand.

claims.statement: Maero are characterised as wild, malevolent and often violent, carrying stone clubs, and covered in dark body hair.
claims.statement_id: Maero digambarkan liar, jahat, dan sering kasar, membawa gada batu sebagai senjata, serta berbulu tubuh gelap.
claims.quote: Maero are characterised as wild, malevolent and often violent, carrying stone clubs as weapons. They are covered in dark body hair

claims.statement: An AA Directions magazine article calls Mount Moehau (also Te Moengahau-o-Tamatekapua) a sacred mountain of the Marutūāhu, a collective of five iwi in the Hauraki region.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah artikel majalah AA Directions menyebut Gunung Moehau (juga Te Moengahau-o-Tamatekapua) sebagai gunung keramat Marutūāhu, gabungan lima iwi di wilayah Hauraki.
claims.quote: Mount Moehau (also called Te Moengahau-o-Tamatekapua, the windy sleeping place of Tamatekapua) is a sacred mountain of the Marutūāhu, a collective of five iwi in the Hauraki region.

claims.statement: The same article says the mountain is said in Māori mythology to be home to both Patupaiarehe and the moehau (or maeroero), a large bipedal creature covered in a thick coat of hair.
claims.statement_id: Artikel yang sama menyebut gunung itu dikatakan dalam mitologi Māori sebagai tempat tinggal Patupaiarehe dan moehau (atau maeroero), makhluk besar berkaki dua yang berbulu lebat.
claims.quote: it is also said in Māori mythology to be home to both Patupaiarehe, fairy-like supernatural beings (he iwi atua), and moehau (or maeroero), a large bipedal creature covered in a thick coat of hair.
